Introducono un 'Anti-Hack score' che ricalcola il punteggio del benchmark marcando come sbagliati tutti gli esempi trapelati.
ov.risultati: ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base fa trapelare il 96% dei problemi di HumanEval con le soluzioni e l'85% delle domande di OpenBookQA con le risposte, contro il 9% e nessuno per DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base. L'Anti-Hack score costa in media 1.5 punti a DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base e 1.3 a Hy3-preview-Base, contro 5 per un altro modello.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe e non riporta limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Esempi di test di un benchmark che finiscono nei dati di addestramento.
Tecnica che fornisce pochi esempi al modello per fargli continuare un testo.
Modello pre-addestrato non ancora ottimizzato per compiti specifici.

2611.20897.abs: Vision models built on Mamba are often explained through their selective step size Delta, on the assumption that a token the scan does not admit cannot influence the prediction. We test that in a concept bottleneck model for lung-nodule malignancy built on a single gated, bidirectional selective state-space block. The answer becomes an interpretability framework: a guarantee, a procedure that checks it, and a pre-registered audit of what it explains. For a fixed gate pattern, masking the input of the causal convolution of the block and giving closed tokens zero weight at readout makes the concept and task logits exactly invariant to the closed tokens. Gating Delta is neither necessary nor sufficient. On LIDC-IDRI, a path-by-path knockout over 15 cross-validated models agrees with this in every run: the largest logit change is exactly 0 whenever the conditions hold and between 4.1 and 6.7 when they do not. The gated model reaches a pooled out-of-fold AUROC of 0.8425 +/- 0.0085, level with an ungated Mamba bottleneck (0.8428). The guarantee belongs to the masked model, not to the gate as an explanation. Post-hoc rankers, which inherit the guarantee on this model, order tokens better than the gate. Gate maps from a model trained on permuted labels are as close to the real maps as two real-label seeds are to each other. Under retraining, the tokens of the gate carry more task information than random tokens and, on shifted crops, more than central ones, but no more than the tokens chosen by hidden attention. We therefore read the gate as a certified support set produced by mask…

ov.problema: I modelli vision basati su Mamba vengono spesso spiegati tramite il loro passo selettivo Delta, assumendo che un token non ammesso dallo scan non possa influenzare la previsione. Questo è importante perché mette in dubbio l'interpretabilità di questi modelli.
ov.idea: Gli autori testano questa ipotesi in un concept bottleneck model per malignità di noduli polmonari basato su un singolo blocco state-space gated e bidirezionale. Dimostrano che, per un pattern di gate fisso, mascherando l'input della convoluzione causale e dando peso zero ai token chiusi al readout, i logit diventano esattamente invarianti ai token chiusi. Il gating di Delta non è né necessario né sufficiente.
ov.risultati: Su LIDC-IDRI, un knockout path-by-path su 15 modelli cross-validati conferma che la massima variazione dei logit è esattamente 0 quando le condizioni valgono e tra 4.1 e 6.7 quando non valgono. Il modello gated raggiunge AUROC out-of-fold pooled di 0.8425 +/- 0.0085, simile a un Mamba bottleneck ungated (0.8428).
ov.limiti: La garanzia appartiene al modello mascherato, non al gate come spiegazione; i ranker post-hoc ordinano i token meglio del gate.

glossario.d: Modello state-space selettivo per sequenze, alternativo ai Transformer.
Rete che prima predice concetti interpretabili, poi usa questi per il task finale.
Area sotto la curva ROC, misura la capacità di discriminare classi.

2611.20371.abs: Linear probing is a common technique in mechanistic interpretability despite the fact that the decodability of a given feature does not necessarily imply the network uses that feature. Intervention faithfulness, not merely decodability, is the appropriate criterion for whether a feature serves a defined active role in the model. Meanwhile, probe regularization has been used for feature discovery, but the impact of regularization on feature causality remains unclear. We study probe regularization systematically, starting with unregularized ordinary least squares (OLS) regression and considering increasing amounts of regularization via ridge regression. We show theoretically that OLS probes amplify low-variance directions in activation space that have spurious correlations with the target feature, whereas regularization reduces influence from these directions. Empirically, we find in a toy transformer and Llama-2-7B that intervention faithfulness increases up to a point, and then decreases again, and that the optimal regularization strength leads to features bearing striking similarity (in both direction and variance) to those learned by optimizing for intervention outcomes directly. Together, these results provide mechanistic justification for regularizing regression probes.

ov.problema: Nell'interpretabilità meccanicistica, la linear probing è comune ma la decodificabilità di una feature non implica che la rete la usi. La fedeltà all'intervento (intervention faithfulness), non solo la decodificabilità, è il criterio appropriato per stabilire se una feature ha un ruolo attivo. L'impatto della regolarizzazione della probe sulla causalità delle feature non è chiaro.
ov.idea: Gli autori studiano sistematicamente la regolarizzazione delle probe, partendo da regressione OLS non regolarizzata e aumentando la regolarizzazione con ridge regression. Teoricamente mostrano che le probe OLS amplificano direzioni a bassa varianza nello spazio delle attivazioni che hanno correlazioni spurie con la feature target, mentre la regolarizzazione riduce l'influenza di queste direzioni. Empiricamente, in un transformer giocattolo e in Llama-2-7B, trovano che la fedeltà all'intervento aumenta fino a un punto e poi diminuisce, e che la forza di regolarizzazione ottimale porta a…
ov.risultati: La fedeltà all'intervento aumenta fino a un punto e poi diminuisce; la regolarizzazione ottimale produce feature simili a quelle ottimizzate per gli interventi.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Tecnica che addestra un classificatore lineare sulle attivazioni per verificare se una feature è decodificabile.
Criterio che verifica se modificare una feature cambia effettivamente il comportamento del modello.
Regressione lineare con penalità L2 che riduce i coefficienti per evitare overfitting.

2611.19774.abs: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map visual observations, robot states, and natural-language instructions to robotic actions, but their multimodal interfaces introduce new security risks. Existing VLA backdoor attacks primarily study trigger-based activation and stealthy action manipulation, leaving conditional suppression of malicious behavior underexplored. We investigate suppression-aware backdoors, which combine conjunctive trigger activation with instruction-conditioned suppression. We instantiate this design through three variants: Cross-Modal Trigger, combining robot-state and spatially separated visual triggers; Self-Suppressing Trigger, requiring a state trigger and a [DISRUPT] instruction token for activation, with [RESTORE] token suppressing the attack; and Multi-Trigger, additionally requiring a visual trigger while retaining suppression even when physical triggers persist. We evaluate these attacks using SmolVLA on two SO-100 manipulation datasets against four baselines: State Backdoor, BadVLA, TabVLA, and SilentDrift. Self-Suppressing and Multi-Trigger reduce Isolation Forest detection from 96--98% to 1--18% and action-space l divergence by 10--14X, achieving 63--71% attack success rates with perfect clean-task performance. Experiments with OpenVLA on LIBERO further show that the attacks transfer to a 7B-parameter policy, evading STRIP and action-distribution-shift detection. Our findings establish conditional suppression as an important dimension for evaluating backdoor threats in VLA policies.

2611.20246.abs: Multi-round diffusion image editing can reduce computation by reusing intermediate activations, but retaining these activations across editing rounds introduces substantial memory and bandwidth overheads. Compression can reduce these overheads, but efficient cache construction is challenging: compressing only after editing requires buffering over 100 GB of activations per request. Moreover, the compressed cache must support selective reuse, as future masked edits require only a subset of the cached activations. It also exposes a scheduling challenge, as cached edits are faster than initial generations, causing naive policies to severely delay either initial generations or editing requests. In this paper, we aim to address both challenges through compression-informed serving. We develop TileCache, a serving system for multi-round diffusion editing. It compresses reusable activations and incorporates a scheduler that balances both edits and initial generation requests. Compared with the state-of-the-art image editing baseline, TileCache sustains over 2x the request arrival rate at 90% SLO attainment. It completes edits 2.4-4.5x and initial generations 1.3-2.2x faster than the baseline, while preserving image quality.

2611.20671.abs: Tamarin-based formal verification of security protocols requires expert-authored multiset rewriting rules and temporal-logic lemmas. Translating a natural-language protocol description into a complete formal model with an LLM is hard because syntactic, reachability, and property-level errors compound across the multi-step modeling process, and a single agent that both authors and self-evaluates cannot reliably localize them. We present MASTA, a multi-agent system that addresses these difficulties through three innovations. First, an operational--evaluative role decomposition assigns rule modeling to an Architect, property modeling to an Auditor, and pure dispatch to a dedicated Arbiter that holds no authoring duties. Second, the Arbiter implements a Tamarin-anchored scheduler that dispatches the next agent based on the latest verifier verdict and routes problem-tagged fixes through a modification list, with a six-class problem taxonomy and an LLM deduplication check preventing routing deadlock. Third, we construct a benchmark of 10 protocols paired with 139 mutation variants and five fine-grained metrics that jointly assess model correctness ($M_1$--$M_3$) and completeness ($M_4$--$M_5$). On this benchmark, MASTA on Qwen 3.5-plus improves over OpenCode on the same backbone by up to $+0.27$ on individual metrics and ranks first on both the correctness and completeness averages, surpassing Codex (GPT-5.5) and Claude Code (Opus 4.7) despite using a weaker LLM. Ablations on five protocols confirm that removing the Arbiter collapses property and verification scores to zero.

2611.20103.abs: MambaVision, a hybrid state-space and attention backbone, places most of its parameters in its widest, fourth stage. We quantified what that stage contributes to multi-label chest radiograph classification. The fourth stage was replaced with lighter single-scan state-space blocks adapted from Spatial-Mamba, with multi-scale dilated depthwise convolutions applied to the scan output; the first three stages were retained. Tiny, Small, and Base models were evaluated across nine dataset-scale combinations drawn from two source cohorts: the National Institutes of Health ChestX-ray14 archive (full ChestMNIST and a high-resolution subset) and Indiana University Open-i. At the Tiny scale, replacement reduced parameter count by 35.7% and increased graphics processing unit throughput by 19.3%; the savings came from the stage's dense projections, not from removing quadratic attention. Without distillation, the mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve on ChestMNIST was 0.004 lower than the baseline (95% bootstrap confidence interval, 0.002 to 0.006), and 0.003 to 0.006 lower across all nine combinations. Knowledge distillation from an unreplaced teacher narrowed the gap to the undistilled baseline to 0.001-0.002 and met the equivalence criterion on ChestMNIST, but distilling the baseline with the same recipe improved it by 0.001-0.003, so a gap of 0.002-0.005 persisted under symmetric training. At the Base scale, the unreplaced Small model was both smaller and more accurate. Fourth-stage replacement is a useful trade-off only for Tiny and Small models. These…

2611.20628.abs: Pixel art is widely used in games and digital content creation, requiring readable forms, coherent spatial relationships, and harmonious colors under limited resolution and palette constraints. Language models show growing promise in visual creation, yet their pixel art creation capabilities lack systematic evaluation. We introduce PixelBench, formalizing text-to-image generation and instruction-guided editing for pixel art and providing a benchmark for these tasks. We further present a creation environment in which language model agents invoke drawing tools through code to generate and edit pixel art. We assess the quality of generated artwork through human evaluation and employ a multimodal large language model as a judge, validating the agreement between its automated assessments and human preferences. We compare language models and configurations across diverse subjects and canvas sizes. In our experiments, GPT-6 Astra achieves both the highest average judge score and the best average human rank, highlighting the potential of general-purpose language models for pixel art creation. We release the tasks, all artworks, the human rankings, and the judge protocol.

2611.21310.abs: Can an AI make a trained language model more mature, in the sense of a better organized latent space, by looking only at the geometry of that space? An analyst model reads a fixed-size digest of topological descriptors of the layers of a frozen target and proposes a transformation, which closed-form ridge regression writes into the feed-forward weights without gradient training. Using lightweight models, 126 runs show that category purity rose on unseen words and sentences, benchmark accuracy stayed within sampling error, and the analyst matched a category-aware heuristic with gentler edits. In a five-model round robin approach, 16 pairs raised purity and four left the target unchanged. The results provide a baseline for future work on LLM-guided, training-free model editing without using raw weights.

2611.20873.abs: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from conversational assistants into autonomous agents embedded in software development workflows, estimating their environmental footprint requires moving beyond conventional token-based accounting. Existing energy estimators focus on isolated request-response interactions, overlooking the repeated processing of accumulated context, cache reuse, and work delegated to subagents. We analyze nearly one billion tokens collected across 42 sessions and 752 task episodes over ten weeks of real-world AI-assisted software development. Cached-context reads make up 94.8% of all API-reported tokens, while uncached input accounts for only 0.017%; for every generated token, approximately 260 cached tokens are read. Context grows 5.3-fold over a session compared with 1.4-fold within individual tasks. To quantify the energy implications, we extend an existing analytical inference-energy model to account for cached-context processing, yielding a cache-aware hybrid estimator. It estimates approximately 250 kWh for the workload, compared with approximately 10 kWh from the output-based estimator EcoLogits, a 25-fold difference largely driven by cached-context reads. Neither estimator has been validated on long cached contexts, but no modeling assumption we varied closes the gap. Starting each task from a fresh context would lower our estimate by about 60%. We also find that parent-session logs report only a subagent's final internal call, undercounting delegated tokens by a factor of ten; for this workload the correction changes the energy estimate by…

ov.problema: Gli agenti LLM nel software engineering consumano energia, ma i modelli esistenti ignorano il riprocessamento del contesto accumulato, il riuso della cache e il lavoro delegato ai subagenti.
ov.idea: Analizzano quasi un miliardo di token da 42 sessioni e 752 episodi in dieci settimane di sviluppo reale. Estendono un modello analitico di energia per includere l'elaborazione del contesto in cache, ottenendo un estimatore ibrido cache-aware.
ov.risultati: Le letture di contesto in cache sono il 94.8% dei token API, l'input non in cache solo lo 0.017%; per ogni token generato si leggono circa 260 token in cache. Il contesto cresce 5.3 volte in una sessione contro 1.4 volte nei task. L'estimatore stima circa 250 kWh contro i circa 10 kWh di EcoLogits, differenza di 25 volte. Partire da contesto fresco ridurrebbe la stima del 60%.
ov.limiti: Nessun estimatore è validato su contesti lunghi in cache; nessuna assunzione variata colma il divario.

glossario.d: riuso di calcoli precedenti per token già visti
token già elaborati e riutilizzati senza ricalcolo
estimatore di energia basato solo sull'output

2611.20321.abs: Vision-based navigation systems for orbit must be trained almost entirely on synthetic imagery, because real labelled images of a given spacecraft in flight rarely exist. Benchmarks like SPEED+ are built for that situation: the training set comes from a simulator, and the test sets are real images of a satellite mockup under two kinds of lighting. That simulator approximates how light reflects off mylar and aluminium, and like every scientific simulator it is misspecified. Its error is radiometric, since it misses the specular highlights, hard shadows and sensor saturation common in real images. We probe the resulting synthetic-to-real gap, the central risk for such systems, with a deliberately simple monocular pose estimator. In a 2x2 study of backbone adaptation and photometric augmentation, trained on synthetic images and tested on both real hardware-in-the-loop domains, we find three things. (1) The model does not know it is failing: regions conformally calibrated to 90% on synthetic data cover only 9-15% of rotation errors on sunlamp and 21-38% on lightbox, so a wrong pose carries the confidence of a correct one. (2) Transfer is asymmetric: scaling data and features improved synthetic rotation error from 1.65 to 1.03 rad but moved the harshly lit sunlamp domain by only 0.05 rad, under twice its seed s.d., whereas adapting the backbone's last stage carried 63-83% of its extra synthetic gain to both real domains. (3) Once the backbone adapts, augmentation helps only in the direction it models: our photometric stack improved the diffusely lit lightbox domain from 1.17 to…

2611.19771.abs: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

ov.problema: I world model JEPA predicono embedding futuri invece di pixel e pianificano nello spazio latente. Due problemi restano: le immagini 2D lasciano implicita la geometria metrica che la manipolazione richiede, e ciò che i modelli immaginano resta nascosto, valutato solo in simulazione con pianificazione latente a breve orizzonte.
ov.idea: JEPA4R è un world model JEPA che osserva nuvole di punti da una singola telecamera di profondità, predice e pianifica nel loro spazio latente, e agisce tramite una testa di policy sui latenti congelati: questa è la pianificazione 4D su punti. Un decoder sul world model congelato mostra ciò che immagina come nuvole di punti 4D.
ov.risultati: L'errore medio dei punti è entro 1,1 cm su 200 passi. Su OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple e Scene supera i modelli JEPA a pixel; su MetaWorld e Adroit Relocate raggiunge il 98,4% e l'88,0%, sopra il secondo classificato R3M (96,0% e 65,3%). Addestrato solo in un gemello digitale, funziona zero-shot su un braccio reale con pinza e mano destra.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta limiti espliciti, ma la valutazione è su specifici benchmark e il trasferimento reale è zero-shot senza fine-tuning.

glossario.d: Architettura che predice rappresentazioni latenti future invece di ricostruire pixel.
Pianificare nello spazio delle rappresentazioni interne anziché nello spazio osservabile.
Capacità di funzionare su un compito nuovo senza addestramento specifico.

2611.20595.abs: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. It tests each result against invariants that any correct API must satisfy and withholds values that break one. We find silent failures in 11 of 15 public research APIs, with counts inflated up to 691 times. Current fixes leave over 70% of answers wrong, and agents report 77.4% of counts a judge flags. Across 7 open models, SilentGuard cuts wrong answers on its target faults from 74.0% to 1.7%, with no loss on fault-free tasks. On three frontier models they fall from 70.2% to 0.5%. A warning from the same check leaves 70.1% wrong, so enforcement is the key. On new fault types, the harness alone cuts wrong answers from 61.1% to 24.5%. It avoids wrong answers by abstaining rather than recovering.

ov.problema: Gli agenti LLM chiamano API e si fidano dei risultati, ma un'API può fallire silenziosamente: ignora parte della richiesta e restituisce HTTP 200 con un risultato plausibile ma sbagliato. I metodi attuali basati su checklist o modelli giudici spesso non se ne accorgono.
ov.idea: SilentGuard sposta la decisione dal modello al sistema che esegue le chiamate (harness). Testa ogni risultato contro invarianti che qualsiasi API corretta deve soddisfare e blocca i valori che violano un'invariante.
ov.risultati: Su 7 modelli open, SilentGuard riduce le risposte sbagliate sui guasti target dal 74.0% all'1.7%, senza perdita su task senza guasti. Su tre modelli frontier scendono dal 70.2% allo 0.5%. Un semplice avviso lascia il 70.1% di risposte sbagliate, quindi l'enforcement è cruciale. Su nuovi tipi di guasto, l'harness da solo riduce le risposte sbagliate dal 61.1% al 24.5%.
ov.limiti: Evita risposte sbagliate astenendosi invece di recuperare il risultato corretto.

glossario.d: Proprietà che deve essere sempre vera per un risultato corretto.
Sistema che esegue e controlla le chiamate agli strumenti.
Errore non segnalato esplicitamente dall'API.

2611.20012.abs: Offline language models could extend access to maternal-health information where internet connectivity is unreliable, but deployment requires both clinically appropriate responses and feasible local execution. This study presents an offline Android assistant integrating ready-made quantized language models, a clinically validated local knowledge package, conversational context, and model-initiated local retrieval. Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3.5 0.8B were compared across 45 conversations and 312 turns per configuration, including a dedicated offline agentic benchmark. Gemma achieved higher response-quality, context-retention, and safety scores; Qwen offered faster generation and lower memory use. Clinician assessment of 150 Gemma responses across nine clinical domains yielded a mean quality score of 3.80/4, with 147 responses meeting the acceptance criterion. A paired RAG-on/off experiment evaluated 74 questions: retrieval improved 11 responses, left 56 neutral, produced four adverse response changes, and left three pairs unassessable. RAG-on had descriptively higher mean usefulness, safety, correctness, and actionability in the conditional 70-pair subset excluding the four flagged pairs from both conditions. Physical-device testing demonstrated offline responses on a 6 GB Android handset, with a 14.3 s median latency, alongside successful reconnection synchronization in the integrated application. Together, the findings document clinical response quality and practical performance of the integrated offline maternal-health assistant.

2611.20623.abs: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models often synthesize policy-violating content, necessitating robust safeguards and rigorous evaluation frameworks. However, current approaches remain largely monolithic in both execution and evaluation, limited to coarse-grained categorization within broad unsafe concepts. Such approaches fail to account for the specific constituent factors of a violation, resulting in weak learning signals and allowing model collapse to bypass safety checks. To overcome these limitations, we propose Example-Based Spatial Guidance (EBSG), a training-free method that utilizes user-editable exemplar packs to provide granular spatial guidance for precise concept steering. Unlike existing methods that coarsely steer the entire image away from a broad concept, EBSG decomposes these categories into specific sub-concepts via exemplar text-image pairs, providing explicit, localized steering signals for more robust safety control. Furthermore, we introduce a vision language model (VLM)-based evaluation protocol that provides a fine-grained assessment, avoiding the pitfall of conventional binary evaluators that permit model collapse to bypass safety checks. Empirically, EBSG achieves state-of-the-art erasure performance across diverse safety datasets and concept categories, spanning four nudity benchmarks, seven I2P harmful-concept slices, and four MJA metaphor categories, while supporting multi-concept removal and transferring to a modern backbone, SD3.

2611.21308.abs: Atomistic machine learning can approximate expensive quantum mechanical calculations at a fraction of their computational cost, but accuracy depends strongly on how the three-dimensional atomic environments are represented. Invariant representations enable fast computation but can fail to distinguish geometrically distinct configurations, especially in highly symmetric environments. We introduce a lightweight benchmark to evaluate expressivity on $n$-fold symmetric configurations, and use it to expose degeneracies in both invariant and equivariant architectures. Guided by these results, we construct a new invariant basis for HIP-HOP which resolves most of the identified failures. On a methane simulation dataset, the extended basis achieves the lowest error among the HIP-HOP variants and has similar accuracy to EquiformerV3 while running $3.2\times$ faster at inference. These results show that carefully constructed invariant representations can mitigate key expressivity limitations while balancing accuracy and computational efficiency.

2611.20853.abs: Motor imagery (MI) enables a brain-computer interface (BCI) to decode movement intentions without overt movement. Hybrid electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) classification combines complementary signals, but inter-subject variability and the design of information exchange between modalities affect generalization to new subjects. We propose a framework that combines Cross-Subject Class Mixup (CSCM) with Selective Attention. CSCM aims to construct new training data to make the model robust against inter-subject variability. It independently selects EEG and fNIRS donor trials from other training subjects within the anchor class and mixes each modality while preserving the original label. Selective Attention provides an effective way to simultaneously model the temporal signal characteristics and fuse the two modalities. It retains causal temporal self-attention for EEG and uses a classification token (CLS) to integrate both modalities, without fNIRS attention updates or direct cross-modal temporal-token attention. Leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) evaluation across 28 subjects on a public EEG-fNIRS dataset yields a mean balanced accuracy (BA) of 76.85% and a macro-averaged F1 score (Macro-F1) of 76.58%. The proposed model achieves the highest mean performance among five reimplemented baselines. We also examine the contributions of CSCM and Selective Attention through modality-specific mixing and donor-policy comparisons, temporal-policy comparisons, interventions on direct cross-modal paths, and component ablations.

2611.19841.abs: Artificial intelligence (AI) scientists pursue discovery through a chain of hypotheses, fitting candidate models to existing observations and often choosing experiments where those models disagree most. Yet when early data miss a narrow feature, model selection favors simple curves that agree across the unmea- sured gap, so disagreement-guided search has no reason to look where the new phenomenon lies. When we tested two frontier AI scientists, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol, across 32 closed-loop trials with a narrow peak omitted from the starting data, both sampled inside the peak region less often than random search. Surprisingly, the agent that followed model disagreement more closely missed the peak in all 32 trials, whereas discovery succeeded when experiments probed the unmeasured gap early and followed up across the anomaly. Asking the right question, rather than testing only where current models disagree, is therefore key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses.

ov.problema: Gli scienziati AI perseguono la scoperta attraverso una catena di ipotesi, adattando modelli candidati alle osservazioni esistenti e scegliendo esperimenti dove i modelli sono più in disaccordo. Ma quando i primi dati mancano una feature stretta, la selezione del modello favorisce curve semplici che concordano nel gap non misurato, quindi la ricerca guidata dal disaccordo non ha motivo di guardare dove si trova il nuovo fenomeno.
ov.idea: Gli autori testano due scienziati AI frontier, Claude Sonnet 5.5 e GPT-6.1-Sol, in 32 trial a ciclo chiuso con un picco stretto omesso dai dati iniziali. Entrambi campionano nella regione del picco meno spesso di una ricerca casuale. Sorprendentemente, l'agente che seguiva più fedelmente il disaccordo tra modelli ha mancato il picco in tutti i 32 trial, mentre la scoperta è riuscita quando gli esperimenti sondavano presto il gap non misurato e seguivano l'anomalia.
ov.risultati: L'agente che seguiva il disaccordo ha mancato il picco in tutti i 32 trial; la scoperta è riuscita quando si sondava presto il gap non misurato.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Processo iterativo in cui si formulano ipotesi, si fanno esperimenti e si aggiornano i modelli.
Differenza nelle previsioni di modelli candidati, usata per scegliere esperimenti informativi.
Modalità in cui l'agente progetta esperimenti, riceve risultati e aggiorna le ipotesi automaticamente.

2611.19676.abs: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of…

2611.20484.abs: SMT solvers expose many configuration choices that determine how well their existing algorithms perform on a workload. We present, to our knowledge, the first workflow that uses general-purpose LLM agents to tune SMT solver configurations. Agents read solver documentation, source code, and persistent experiment records to propose option changes, and a deterministic harness measures each proposal, validates the returned models, and selects changes separately for each competition Division. Over roughly nine weeks, our tuning campaign recorded 4,545 proposals for cvc5 across 13 Divisions and 36 logics. We evaluate the tuned configurations on the 2026 and 2025 SMT-COMP ModelValidation benchmarks under a 24-second cutoff. On problems not used for training, they validate more problems than official cvc5 in ten of the 13 Divisions in 2026 and in eight in 2025, with geometric-mean gains of 7.8% and 6.8% across Divisions. On the complete official selections, which include training problems, the tuned floating-point counts exceed those of every individual competition participant in both years. Further studies show how configuration changes make existing algorithms effective by changing access to strategies, scheduling, and option compatibility, and how benchmark families trade off against one another. The agents' experiment traces contain hypothesis-based proposals in every tuning group, and 64.3% of the extracted hypotheses draw on prior measurements. These results show that agent-guided tuning can specialize a mature SMT solver and that accumulated experimental evidence informs…

2611.19896.abs: Looped language models such as Ouro and Raven apply one weight-shared block several times per token, so autoregressive decoding (AR) runs every loop of every token in sequence. Pipelined self-speculative decoders overlap these loops by drafting tokens from shallow readouts and verifying them at full depth. Yet every loop of a looped LM ends in a readout of the next token, and draft tokens pass through every depth anyway, so each depth can check them without an extra pass. We introduce LoopSkim, in which the depth of the pipeline is the verifier. Draft tokens copied from the context, as in prompt lookup decoding, enter after the first loops, any later readout that contradicts one replaces it at that depth, and only full-depth readouts commit tokens. LoopSkim fixes the random draws of every position in advance, so each check compares two tokens and decoding stays lossless in exact arithmetic under sampling for any number of checks and draft chains. Without training, its speedup over AR averages 1.73x that of LoopSpec across greedy decoding and sampling, and its checks between the first loops and full depth speed it up on every model. An optional draft head adds a second chain and raises this average to 1.99x.

ov.problema: I modelli linguistici 'looped' (come Ouro e Raven) applicano più volte lo stesso blocco di pesi per ogni token, quindi la decodifica autoregressiva esegue in sequenza ogni iterazione (loop) di ogni token. Questo è lento.
ov.idea: LoopSkim sfrutta il fatto che ogni loop termina con una lettura del token successivo e che i token bozza passano comunque attraverso ogni profondità. I token bozza copiati dal contesto entrano dopo i primi loop; ogni lettura successiva che li contraddice li sostituisce a quella profondità; solo le letture a piena profondità confermano i token. Le estrazioni casuali sono fissate in anticipo, quindi la decodifica resta lossless (senza perdita) in aritmetica esatta anche con campionamento.
ov.risultati: Senza addestramento, lo speedup medio rispetto alla decodifica autoregressiva è 1,73 volte quello di LoopSpec su greedy e campionamento; con una testa bozza opzionale sale a 1,99 volte.
ov.limiti: Richiede modelli looped con letture intermedie; i guadagni dipendono dal modello e dalla configurazione.

glossario.d: Tecnica che genera bozze veloci e le verifica con il modello completo.
Senza perdita di qualità: l'output è identico a quello della decodifica normale.
Modello che riusa lo stesso blocco di pesi più volte per token.

2611.21307.abs: Causal abstraction explains a frozen network by aligning its activations with the variables of a simpler, interpretable model, and checking that interventions on the two agree. Finding such an alignment currently requires a counterfactual dataset: for every pair of prompts, the answer the network ought to give once the variable has been changed. In practice, those labels are produced by an executable algorithm for the behavior, written before studying the model supposed to implement it. However, the criterion these methods optimize only leverages the answer an intervention should produce. Here, we develop an approach that lets the investigator define that relationship directly: the answers the variable can produce, and which of them an intervention should yield. We call this interface a semantic program and introduce Programmable Semantic Interventions (PSI): a low-rank activation subspace learned so that interchanging it changes the model's answer as the program declares, with the expected answers read from the frozen model itself. On the MIB benchmark PSI performs on par with supervised alignment at matched data and training budget, without curated pairs, and it needs no ground-truth labels; while on natural science questions with gold labels withheld, it tracks the model's own answers better than a subspace trained on gold labels. The declaration also fixes a coordinate system with known semantics, enabling donor-free steering: jointly training PSI for both localization and control realizes 94.8% of held-out requests for answers the investigator chooses, without the…

ov.problema: L'astrazione causale spiega una rete congelata allineando le sue attivazioni alle variabili di un modello interpretabile più semplice, ma trovare tale allineamento richiede un dataset controfattuale: per ogni coppia di prompt, la risposta che la rete dovrebbe dare una volta cambiata la variabile. In pratica queste etichette sono prodotte da un algoritmo eseguibile per il comportamento, scritto prima di studiare il modello.
ov.idea: Gli autori sviluppano un approccio che permette al ricercatore di definire direttamente quella relazione: le risposte che la variabile può produrre e quali di esse un intervento dovrebbe dare. Chiamano questa interfaccia 'programma semantico' e introducono Programmable Semantic Interventions (PSI): un sottospazio di attivazione a basso rango appreso in modo che scambiarlo cambi la risposta del modello come dichiara il programma, con le risposte attese lette dal modello congelato stesso.
ov.risultati: Sul benchmark MIB PSI si comporta come l'allineamento supervisionato a parità di dati e budget di training, senza coppie curate e senza etichette ground-truth; su domande di scienze naturali con etichette oro nascoste, segue le risposte del modello meglio di un sottospazio addestrato su etichette oro. La dichiarazione fissa anche un sistema di coordinate con semantica nota, abilitando steering senza donatore.

glossario.d: spiegare una rete allineandola a un modello più semplice e verificando gli interventi
insieme di direzioni con poche dimensioni effettive
modificare il comportamento del modello intervenendo sulle attivazioni

2611.19826.abs: Open-weight model hubs now ship not only chat checkpoints but a long tail of derivatives---fine-tunes, safety guards, vision--language models (VLMs), audio wrappers, and generative heads---yet residual-stream safety audits still often intervene at a single site, usually the text decoder $T$. We ask a localization question under one shared mean / rank-1 difference-in-means (DiM) extract$=$intervene protocol, with matched-norm random and empty-rate controls: does causal chat attack lift concentrate at $T$, or do perceptual encoders, projectors, and fusion paths ($E$/$P$/$F$) supply a comparable bypass? On the mixed-input settings we stress-test---HADES adversarial images paired with harmful text prompts, and spoken AdvBench via text-to-speech (TTS) or silence---text DiM at $T$ raises attack success rate (ASR) while the same mean DiM at $E$/$P$/$F$ does not; attacks track harmful text rather than image or audio content. Margin-rank and leverage probes on a Vision leaf show that this recipe is extremal at $T$ and near chance at $P$/$E$, which pressures a weak-extractor reading of those flat cells for the DiM family we study. Catalog breadth and mapper-free base$\to$derivative transfer when residual widths match provide supporting coverage under the same gates; generative U-Nets are a separate band under generation judges. The primary claim is this recipe-scoped $T$ vs.\ non-text intervenability asymmetry---intervention accessibility under mean / rank-1 DiM, not a claim that refusal is absent or fully represented outside $T$ (text vs.\ perceptual contrasts and pooling differ by…

ov.problema: I modelli open-weight includono non solo checkpoint di chat ma una lunga coda di derivati (fine-tune, guardie di sicurezza, modelli visione-linguaggio, wrapper audio, teste generative), eppure gli audit di sicurezza sul flusso residuo spesso intervengono in un singolo sito, di solito il decoder testuale T. Gli autori chiedono se l'attacco causale di chat si concentra su T o se encoder percettivi, proiettori e percorsi di fusione (E/P/F) forniscono un bypass comparabile.
ov.idea: Usano un protocollo condiviso di estrazione e intervento basato su differenza di medie / rango-1 (DiM), con controlli di norme abbinate e tasso vuoto. Testano su input misti: immagini avversariali HADES con prompt testuali dannosi, e AdvBench parlato via text-to-speech o silenzio. La DiM testuale su T aumenta il tasso di successo dell'attacco (ASR) mentre la stessa DiM media su E/P/F no; gli attacchi seguono il testo dannoso piuttosto che il contenuto di immagini o audio. Sonde di rango-margine e leva su una foglia Vision mostrano che questa ricetta è estrema su T e vicina al caso su P/E.
ov.risultati: La DiM testuale su T aumenta l'ASR; la stessa su E/P/F no. La ricetta è estrema su T e vicina al caso su P/E.
ov.limiti: La rivendicazione principale è un'asimmetria di intervenibilità T vs non-testo limitata a questa ricetta (media / rango-1 DiM), non un'affermazione generale sul rifiuto.

glossario.d: Tecnica che estrae una direzione nel flusso residuo come differenza tra medie di attivazioni positive e negative.
Percentuale di attacchi che riescono a far generare al modello contenuti dannosi.
Sequenza di attivazioni interne di un transformer, usata per analisi di interpretabilità e sicurezza.

2611.20430.abs: LLM-based agents can automate model post-training, accelerating progress toward recursive self-improvement. Despite their promise, existing approaches remain under-explored and face two main challenges: (1) strategy lock-in that limits exploration beyond the initial strategy; and (2) coupled execution that obscures the effects of individual modifications. To address these challanges, we propose TrainExplorer, a multi-agent framework for autonomous post-training, that incorporates strategy planning and execution decoupling, to achieve broaden strategy exploration. First, strategy planning draws on scientific literature to construct a candidate search space of training strategies. Then, decoupled execution enables single-component interventions and attribution to guide strategy exploration. Extensive experiments on PostTrainBench demonstrate that TrainExplorer achieves a weighted aggregate score of 39.02, outperforming Claude Code using the same LLM by 7.32 and surpassing GPT-5.6 Sol-powered Codex, which scores 36.23. Code will be available.

2611.19823.abs: Reflective skill optimizers improve multi-turn LLM agents by revising instructions from failed and successful rollouts, yet accumulating edge-case rules bloats prompts, inflates token use, and pushes agents into long, error-prone loops. We introduce EfficientSkill, a two-step framework that first discovers a reliable skill without token penalties, and then warm-starts accuracy-guarded pruning from that skill to compress instructions, bound agent turns, and offload reusable code into workspace utilities with zero implementation prompt cost. Across four frontier, mid-tier, and open-weight models on MATH-500, ALFWorld, and SpreadsheetBench, EfficientSkill cuts output tokens over unconstrained EvoSkill on 11 of 12 configurations (by up to 80%) while raising mean accuracy on every benchmark, including +14.3 and +17.5 percentage-point gains on SpreadsheetBench with Gemini 3.8 Flash and Grok 4.1 Fast by replacing stalled loops with compact workflows. By shrinking both generated tokens and replayed history, EfficientSkill lowers total token usage and serving cost across every evaluated configuration, with or without full-prefix KV caching.

ov.problema: Gli ottimizzatori riflessivi di skill migliorano gli agenti LLM multi-turno rivedendo le istruzioni da rollout falliti e riusciti, ma accumulare regole per casi limite gonfia i prompt, aumenta l'uso di token e spinge gli agenti in loop lunghi e soggetti a errori.
ov.idea: Introducono EfficientSkill, un framework in due passi: prima scopre una skill affidabile senza penalità di token, poi avvia da quella skill un pruning protetto dall'accuratezza per comprimere le istruzioni, limitare i turni dell'agente e spostare codice riutilizzabile in utility di workspace con costo zero nel prompt.
ov.risultati: Su quattro modelli (frontier, mid-tier e open-weight) e tre benchmark (MATH-500, ALFWorld, SpreadsheetBench), EfficientSkill riduce i token di output rispetto a EvoSkill non vincolato in 11 delle 12 configurazioni (fino all'80%) aumentando l'accuratezza media su ogni benchmark, inclusi guadagni di +14,3 e +17,5 punti percentuali su SpreadsheetBench con Gemini 3.8 Flash e Grok 4.1 Fast, sostituendo loop bloccati con workflow compatti. Riduce anche l'uso totale di token e il costo di servizio in ogni configurazione valutata, con o senza KV caching completo del prefisso.

glossario.d: Istruzioni o procedure apprese che guidano il comportamento dell'agente.
Sequenza di interazioni dell'agente usata per valutare o addestrare.
Memorizzazione di chiavi e valori già calcolati per velocizzare generazioni successive.

2611.21299.abs: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing mathematical discovery, moving beyond benchmark-level problem solving to tackle frontier research problems. This progress is ushering mathematics into an era of proof abundance, raising a fundamental challenge: how can we ensure the correctness of the ever-growing volume of AI-generated proofs and transform them into trustworthy, machine-verified mathematical knowledge? We introduce Turing Agent, an agent harness designed to orchestrate end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics. Its wo-scale architecture integrates theorem formalization and proof formalization agents, empowered by structured proof decomposition, parallel verification, accumulated proof experience, and selective semantic review. Leveraging our collaborations with theoretical computer science (TCS) researchers, we focus our evaluation on TCS, a particularly demanding domain characterized by intricate quantification, complex dependencies, and stringent semantic requirements. Against direct generation and general-purpose coding harnesses, including Codex CLI and Claude Code, Turing Agent achieves approximately 57-62% faithful formalization success on Formal TCS Bench and 83% overall pass@1 on a TCS-focused subset of RLMEval, using GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Notably, Turing Agent, built on DeepSeek, successfully completes the formal verification of three previously unresolved TCS tasks from OpenAI's October 2026 collection. One particularly challenging TCS problem required about a hundred formally verified auxiliary claims. Moreover, by…

2611.19822.abs: Video world models promise to predict the future of a scene from its present. Do current models keep this promise? We probe this question counterfactually. When a small change to the present flips the future, such as a box resting a few millimeters before or past a table edge, a model that tracks the state of the world must flip its prediction too. We build FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks. At the base, visual minimal pairs, two nearly identical frames whose true futures differ, test whether predictions change across the boundary; matched controls go further and test whether they change only where the future does; and dense sweeps, the strictest level, locate exactly where they change. All 11 video world models we evaluate fall short. The best averages 18.3% pair accuracy over real and simulated scenes, below the 25% of random guessing. Models flip as often on steps that leave the future unchanged as on steps that change it, and their response stays flat across the sweeps. On the same frames, a vision-language model is selective and traces a near S-shaped curve near the boundary, and a coding agent that measures the image comes close to the true boundary. This implies that the deciding information is in the frame, and video models just miss it. We therefore urge the community to rethink world modeling as pure video prediction. Next-frame prediction must do more than draw plausible pixels; it must also identify the causal states that control future dynamics.

2611.20306.abs: Safety filters for heterogeneous robot teams fail because of missing constraints, overestimated braking capabilities and conflicts between individually satisfiable constraints. We present OntoCBF, which compiles a domain ontology with a class taxonomy, typed relations, safety axioms and a dynamics profile per robot class into a control barrier function filter with one quadratic program per agent. Description-logic entailment supplies the constraints of any team online, including those that follow from chains of relations and from classes defined by what a robot carries, so the existing safety axioms cover new robot classes, payload classes and combinations. We prove that a subclass may reuse the braking capability of its parent whenever it can produce every velocity of the parent, a property separate from subsumption. For box-bounded double integrators this property is also necessary, and every loss of safety then begins with a conflict. Once three robots interact, the safe set of pairwise barriers contains states from which a collision is unavoidable, and such states persist in larger teams under any fixed capability reduction. In a simulated warehouse where humans ignore the robots, a filter written for the design classes violates safety in 89-100 % of the episodes with unseen classes. In all scenarios, including one with 32 robots, OntoCBF violates safety in 20-70 % of the episodes, each time after a conflict, with a median deepest intrusion of 10-17 % of the keep-out distance. A multi-agent PPO policy trained with the filter in the loop lowers the rate of infeasible…

2611.19800.abs: Transformer language models are commonly scaled by making their blocks wider or stacking them deeper. In this work, we explore a complementary path: branching, the parallel composition of full Transformer blocks. We introduce the Multi-Branch Transformer (MBT), which processes the input through shared initial layers, executes independently parameterized branches of sequential blocks in parallel, and fuses their outputs before shared final layers. At comparable training compute, we study three MBT variants: Wide-Shallow preserves block width, Narrow-Deep preserves sequential depth, and Balanced interpolates between them. In controlled pretraining experiments at four mixture-of-experts scales (0.8B to 2.1B total parameters), 2-branch Wide-Shallow MBTs consistently outperform sequential Transformers under matched parameter and training-compute budgets. Balanced MBTs improve further and retain comparable quality as the number of branches increases. To improve inference efficiency at long contexts, we introduce Joint-KV, which constructs a shared KV cache from branch representations at each depth. Our final recipe combines Balanced MBTs with Joint-KV, supported by an inference engine that exploits branch grouping and shared-cache reuse. Fitted scaling curves indicate that standard Transformers require up to 1.26x as much training body compute to match our final models' validation loss. These models reduce full-model KV-cache storage by up to 34% and deliver up to 51.4% higher decoding throughput on a single H200 GPU. Ablation studies show that branching yields gains beyond…

ov.problema: I Transformer vengono di solito scalati allargando i blocchi o impilandoli in profondità; qui si esplora una terza via, il branching (composizione parallela di blocchi interi), per capire se può dare migliori compromessi tra qualità e costo.
ov.idea: Il Multi-Branch Transformer (MBT) passa l'input attraverso layer iniziali condivisi, poi esegue in parallelo rami di blocchi con parametri indipendenti e infine fonde gli output prima dei layer finali condivisi. Si studiano tre varianti (Wide-Shallow, Narrow-Deep, Balanced) e si introduce Joint-KV, che costruisce una KV cache condivisa dalle rappresentazioni dei rami a ogni profondità per migliorare l'inferenza su contesti lunghi.
ov.risultati: A parità di parametri e compute di training, i MBT Wide-Shallow a 2 rami battono i Transformer sequenziali; i Balanced migliorano ulteriormente e mantengono qualità simile all'aumentare dei rami. Le curve di scaling indicano che i Transformer standard richiedono fino a 1.26x più compute di training per eguagliare la validation loss dei modelli finali; la KV cache è ridotta fino al 34% e il decoding è fino al 51.4% più veloce.
ov.limiti: Gli esperimenti sono limitati a pretraining controllato su scala ridotta (0.8B-2.1B parametri totali) e a varianti con 2 rami per i risultati principali.

glossario.d: Composizione parallela di più blocchi Transformer completi invece di allargarli o impilarli.
Memoria che conserva chiavi e valori già calcolati per evitare di ricalcolarli durante la generazione.
Curve che mettono in relazione prestazioni e risorse di training (parametri, compute).

2611.19747.abs: Vision models are sensitive to object-background context, yet it remains unclear how recognition changes as the semantic distance between objects and backgrounds increases. We introduce ImageNet-OOC1k, a benchmark enabling graded control of object-background relationships along a continuous consensus visual-semantic dissimilarity axis. This formulation reveals a highly consistent monotonic decline in recognition accuracy across 35 models spanning convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, and vision-language models. Internal analyses of Vision Transformers reveal patterns consistent with aggregation failure, where object evidence is present at the patch level but not consolidated into the final prediction. Using this characterization as a diagnostic probe, a simple spatial re-ranking strategy recovers a subset of these errors and improves in-sample accuracy by up to 5.7 percentage points. These results establish context sensitivity as a continuous and predictable property of modern vision systems, with Vision Transformer analyses suggesting that aggregation limitations may contribute to some failure types even when object evidence remains available.

2611.20202.abs: Sim-to-real RL has achieved impressive results in dexterous manipulation but remains limited to tasks with accurate rigid-body simulation. However, these methods cannot be applied to skills that involve deformable and particles, with which the simulation speed will become too slow for large-scale RL learning. We present DAPPT, a sim-to-real framework for end-to-end dexterous tool-use manipulation skills, e.g., sand scooping, play-dough rod-rolling, without simulating non-rigid materials. Our method learns a domain-aware RL policy by tracking procedural trajectories parameterized by domain parameters, and distills it into an end-to-end domain-aware sensorimotor policy. Furthermore, explicit domain represen-tation enables fast selection of domain parameters that can maximize downstream task performance. We evaluate DAPPT end-to-end on six dexterous manipulation tasks, including sand scooping, play-dough rod-rolling, sand scraping, mouse-wheel scrolling, dispenser pressing, and spray triggering. Our method achieves 1.5-3.8x in task metrics through the best domain parameter and transfers zero-shot to the real world.

2611.19745.abs: Recent efforts to improve the efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have explored visual token pruning, quantization, and feature compression. However, the properties that determine whether transformed visual tokens remain usable by a frozen decoder are not well characterized. We introduce \textbf{TIVS (Token Identity Versus Statistics)}, a training-free intervention framework that separately studies sequence permutation, token retention, numerical precision, and statistical replacement under controlled conditions. On 192 POPE questions, three token permutations change TinyLLaVA accuracy by only $-0.17$ percentage points on average, while changing 4.69\% of individual predictions. Diagonal and rank-64 Gaussian replacements decrease accuracy by 25.0 and 28.1 points on the same subset. Further experiments with exact moment constraints, quantization error, token retention, and additional visual tasks reveal how strongly the effects depend on the original feature values and the evaluation setting. These findings provide an empirical basis for assessing visual token transformations in frozen MLLMs and designing more reliable multimodal interfaces.

ov.problema: Nei modelli multimodali (MLLM) si trasformano i token visivi per ridurre i costi (pruning, quantizzazione, compressione), ma non è chiaro quali proprietà rendano i token trasformati ancora utilizzabili da un decoder congelato (fisso).
ov.idea: TIVS è un framework di intervento senza addestramento che studia separatamente permutazione di sequenza, ritenzione dei token, precisione numerica e sostituzione statistica in condizioni controllate. Usa sostituzioni diagonali e gaussiane a rango 64 per testare quanto contano i valori originali delle feature.
ov.risultati: Su 192 domande POPE, tre permutazioni dei token cambiano l'accuratezza di TinyLLaVA di solo -0,17 punti percentuali in media, ma cambiano il 4,69% delle predizioni individuali. Sostituzioni diagonali e gaussiane a rango 64 riducono l'accuratezza di 25,0 e 28,1 punti sullo stesso sottoinsieme.
ov.limiti: I risultati dipendono fortemente dai valori originali delle feature e dal setting di valutazione; non è una soluzione ma uno studio empirico.

glossario.d: Modello linguistico multimodale che elabora testo e immagini.
Rappresentazioni numeriche di parti dell'immagine usate dal modello.
Parte del modello i cui pesi non vengono aggiornati.

2611.19684.abs: Diffusion-based driving planners can generate multiple trajectories for the same scene, but these candidates vary in quality. Can their internal states reveal which candidate will be better before denoising is complete? We systematically study this question in three pretrained planners: Alpamayo, ReCogDrive-IL, and HDP, using linear probes to predict final trajectory quality from intermediate states and evaluating candidate ranking and selection on held-out scenes. Across all three planners, we observe that states from the first denoiser evaluation already support informative selection, while further denoising does not consistently improve selection quality. Further analyses show that readout depends on the representation and reader, and that selection can coexist with limited overall ranking accuracy. These findings motivate an early-selection method that selects after the first denoiser evaluation and completes only the chosen candidate. This reduces computation relative to fully denoising every candidate and improves open-loop trajectory quality over random selection across all three planners. In particular, it reduces Alpamayo's average displacement error by 17.8% and 13.4% in one- and four-camera configurations, respectively. Closed-loop evaluations also show higher mean driving scores and progress.

2611.20078.abs: On-ramp merging is a typical safety and throughput problem on highways. Without proper coordination, human drivers and self-interested autonomous vehicles may make risky manoeuvres and cause accidents or congestion. With recent advances in connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), vehicles can be trained to coordinate for safe and efficient merging. However, in dense traffic, forming an effective observation of the traffic state is challenging. For example, observing only the neighbouring vehicles may lead to locally optimal decisions, while observing the entire traffic can introduce much irrelevant information. In this paper, we propose a transformer-based MARL vehicle control model to address these problems. A roadside infrastructure controller receives the states of all CAVs via vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication and sends control commands back to them. An attention-based observation encoder is designed where each vehicle can filter the relevant vehicle information from the global traffic state. The proposed model is evaluated in SUMO against three baselines: a model that observes only the neighbouring vehicles, a model that encodes the global traffic information, and the rule-based SUMO model. The results show that our model achieves the highest traffic flow, safety and smoothness. Furthermore, in a four-hour simulation with dynamic traffic demand, our model successfully avoids traffic jams, while other baseline models fail at high traffic flow. We also show that our model remains effective when human-driven vehicles…

2611.19499.abs: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from a covariance-adjusted discriminant to the mean difference, and evaluate probing and additive steering, which adds the direction to the hidden state, along the family at a fixed side effect. For truthfulness and sentiment, in every model, the best probe is not the best steering direction: steering consistently favors directions closer to the mean difference. This separation holds across 59 of 60 layer-model-concept combinations in a layer sweep, with matched probe and steering texts in all six model-concept combinations, and under a rotation-based steering operator. The exact steering optimum is less stable: for sentiment, an intermediate direction produces a 27-56% stronger steering effect than the mean difference, but this gain shrinks or disappears with matched texts and depends on the layer and the operator. The two roles also transfer differently across models. A probe transferred by a linear map fitted on neutral text retains 81-91% of the target model's above-chance probing performance, while the transferred mean difference retains less of its steering effect in 11 of 12 model pairs. This is a consistent tendency, although our predefined criteria classify…

ov.problema: Le direzioni di probing (rilevare un concetto) e steering (cambiare il comportamento) sono spesso usate in modo intercambiabile, ma non è chiaro se la direzione migliore per una lo sia anche per l'altra.
ov.idea: Gli autori costruiscono una famiglia di direzioni da discriminante aggiustato per covarianza a differenza delle medie, e valutano probing e steering additivo a parità di effetti collaterali. Scoprono che la direzione migliore per probing non è la migliore per steering.
ov.risultati: In 59 su 60 combinazioni layer-modello-concetto, lo steering preferisce direzioni vicine alla differenza delle medie. Per il sentiment, una direzione intermedia produce un effetto di steering 27-56% più forte, ma il guadagno diminuisce con testi appaiati. Il trasferimento tra modelli mantiene l'81-91% della performance di probing ma meno per lo steering.
ov.limiti: L'optimum esatto per lo steering è meno stabile e dipende da layer e operatore.

glossario.d: Tecnica per verificare se un concetto è rappresentato negli stati nascosti.
Modifica degli stati nascosti per cambiare il comportamento del modello.
Direzione che separa meglio due classi di dati.

2611.19982.abs: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration. The system supports natural language to GraphQL translation, GraphQL schema generation, schema mapping, trace data lifecycle management and multi-tool workflows for reliability engineering. Its agents are instrumented with agent analytics, so that their model and tool calls can be traced. We evaluate each agent on its own benchmark, scored against gold answers where they exist and by a model judge for schema mapping and chart quality. Query generation on a public benchmark and routing work well with a current open model, and the data lifecycle management agent solves most of its scenarios. The evaluation exposed defects that only appear when prompts, parsers and serving stacks are tested together, and we report them together with their fixes.

2611.19455.abs: Speculative decoding lets a cheap draft model propose tokens that a large language model verifies in a single forward pass. When the verifier keeps a KV cache, verification is cheap and drafting must be nearly free. Session-local drafters, which predict from the prompt and the text generated so far, meet that bar without training. We compare a recency-weighted, backing-off, confidence-gated session memory against prompt lookup decoding in its reference form, which copies from the earliest earlier match, and in a variant that copies from the most recent one, with paired per-prompt bootstrap intervals throughout. On general, medical, and legal text with a Mistral-7B verifier, recency accounts for the speed: most-recent lookup gains up to 0.09 in speedup over earliest-match lookup on 500-token generations, and session memory's weighting and backoff add nothing measurable on top, at 30 to 40 times the drafting cost. Energy tells a different story. On medical and legal text, unselective drafters are 14% faster than plain decoding yet use as much energy per token, while drafters that abstain on weak evidence save 3 to 4 joules per 100 tokens; a three-token minimum match length on prompt lookup matches the confidence-gated session memory. Outputs are token-identical to greedy decoding in 94% of generations, with every divergence at a numerical near-tie. Under a repetition penalty, long-generation speedups shrink from 1.4-1.7x to 1.1-1.2x, but recency still helps and the length floor is the only drafter that saves energy in both domains.

ov.problema: La decodifica speculativa permette a un modello draft economico di proporre token che un modello grande verifica in un singolo forward pass. Quando il verificatore ha una KV cache, la verifica è economica e il drafting deve essere quasi gratuito. I drafter session-locali, che predicono dal prompt e dal testo generato, soddisfano questo requisito senza addestramento.
ov.idea: Gli autori confrontano una memoria di sessione con peso di recency, backing-off e gating di confidenza contro prompt lookup decoding nella sua forma di riferimento (copia dalla prima corrispondenza precedente) e in una variante che copia dalla più recente. Usano intervalli bootstrap appaiati per prompt.
ov.risultati: Su testo generale, medico e legale con verificatore Mistral-7B, la recency spiega l'aumento di velocità: il lookup più recente guadagna fino a 0.09 in speedup rispetto al lookup della prima corrispondenza su generazioni di 500 token. La ponderazione e il backoff della memoria di sessione non aggiungono nulla di misurabile, con un costo di drafting 30-40 volte superiore. Sul testo medico e legale, i drafter non selettivi sono il 14% più veloci della decodifica semplice ma usano la stessa energia per token, mentre i drafter che si astengono su prove deboli risparmiano 3-4 joule per 100 token.…
ov.limiti: Sotto una penalità di ripetizione, gli speedup per generazioni lunghe si riducono da 1.4-1.7x a 1.1-1.2x, ma la recency aiuta ancora.

glossario.d: Tecnica in cui un modello piccolo propone token e uno grande li verifica in blocco.
Memoria delle chiavi e valori già calcolati, evita ricalcoli durante la generazione.
Fattore di accelerazione rispetto a un metodo di riferimento.

2611.19403.abs: A language model's confidence on a physics problem deserves trust only if it ignores details irrelevant to the answer. We introduce DECOY (Distractor-Embedded Certified cOunterfactuals for phYsics): 155 families of four prompts differing in one irrelevant detail. A symbolic solver certifies that each edit preserves the answer. Families are labelled by the largest drop in the model's log-probability of the certified answer, using a threshold fixed before probe training. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is sensitive on 50.0% of the 140 families yielding labels, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 22.9%. Effects are largest when distractor values lie numerically close to the answer. A linear probe on Qwen's layer-18 hidden state, averaged over four renderings, predicts sensitivity before generation at AUROC 0.760 with whole families held out. A separately tuned single-rendering probe reaches 0.747. A frozen layer-16 probe reaches 0.820 pooled AUROC on 15 families built after training, though within-cue-type AUROC is lower (0.667-0.6875). Under a paired family bootstrap, the probe performs on par with a fitted token-entropy baseline (AUROC 0.727) and achieves the lowest Brier score among tested predictors (0.204 versus 0.214). Knocking out four attention heads at layer 16 cancels sensitivity on a 20-family panel, localising it to a narrow mechanism. These results show that Qwen's confidence can track irrelevant details, that this failure is detectable before generation, and that targeted intervention can suppress it. DECOY provides certified ground truth and paired-tested baselines for evaluating…

ov.problema: La fiducia di un modello linguistico su un problema di fisica è affidabile solo se ignora dettagli irrilevanti per la risposta. Serve un modo per misurare e prevedere se il modello è sensibile a distrattori (dettagli inutili).
ov.idea: DECOY crea 155 famiglie di quattro prompt che differiscono per un solo dettaglio irrilevante, verificato da un risolutore simbolico. Le famiglie sono etichettate in base alla massima caduta di log-probabilità della risposta corretta. Una sonda lineare sullo stato nascosto del layer 18 di Qwen predice la sensibilità prima della generazione.
ov.risultati: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct è sensibile sul 50,0% delle 140 famiglie etichettate, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct sul 22,9%. La sonda su Qwen raggiunge AUROC 0,760 con famiglie tenute fuori; una sonda congelata al layer 16 arriva a 0,820 AUROC su 15 famiglie nuove, ma entro lo stesso tipo di cue è più bassa (0,667-0,6875). Disattivare quattro teste di attenzione al layer 16 annulla la sensibilità su un pannello di 20 famiglie.
ov.limiti: La sonda ha prestazioni simili a una baseline di entropia dei token e AUROC più bassa entro lo stesso tipo di cue; i risultati sono su modelli specifici.

glossario.d: Misura della capacità di distinguere due classi; 1 è perfetto, 0,5 è caso.
Classificatore semplice addestrato su rappresentazioni interne del modello.
Logaritmo della probabilità assegnata dal modello a una risposta.

2611.19446.abs: Depth recurrence increases effective model depth by repeatedly applying a fixed computation block. However, sharing attention parameters does not share the key-value (KV) states generated at different recurrence iterations, which causes memory growth with recurrence depth during autoregressive decoding. We study how to reduce this memory cost through architectural and cache-sharing approaches within a common depth-recurrent framework. We first study a looped hybrid that repeats a stack of Transformer layers, with recurrent mLSTM or Gated DeltaNet blocks replacing most attention layers and periodic Transformer attention anchors retained. We then restrict recurrence to a dedicated recurrent workspace in a Parcae-style architecture and test its stabilising adapter as a wrapper for the looped hybrid. Finally, we train a looped Transformer with recurrent KV replay, where only selected recurrence iterations write KV states that later iterations reuse. This trains the model to operate with the same shared KV topology used during inference. We find that looped hybrids require sufficiently frequent attention anchors, with performance depending strongly on the recurrent mixer. For cross-iteration KV sharing, recurrent KV replay allows multiple recurrence iterations to reuse the same KV states while retaining performance close to the full looped Transformer with separate KV caches for each iteration.

ov.problema: I modelli a ricorrenza di profondità (depth-recurrent) applicano più volte lo stesso blocco, aumentando la profondità effettiva. Ma condividere i parametri di attenzione non condivide gli stati KV generati a iterazioni diverse, causando crescita di memoria con la profondità durante la decodifica autoregressiva.
ov.idea: Gli autori studiano approcci architetturali e di condivisione della cache in un framework comune. Testano un ibrido looped con blocchi mLSTM o Gated DeltaNet che sostituiscono la maggior parte dei layer di attenzione, mantenendo ancore di attenzione Transformer periodiche. Poi limitano la ricorrenza a un workspace dedicato in stile Parcae e usano un adattatore stabilizzante. Infine addestrano un Transformer looped con 'recurrent KV replay': solo alcune iterazioni scrivono stati KV che le iterazioni successive riusano.
ov.risultati: Gli ibridi looped richiedono ancore di attenzione sufficientemente frequenti, con prestazioni che dipendono molto dal mixer ricorrente. Il recurrent KV replay permette a più iterazioni di riusare gli stessi stati KV mantenendo prestazioni vicine a quelle del Transformer looped completo con cache KV separate per ogni iterazione.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta numeri specifici di prestazioni o memoria; i risultati sono qualitativi e dipendono dalla frequenza delle ancore di attenzione.

glossario.d: Ripetere lo stesso blocco di calcolo per aumentare la profondità effettiva.
Riuso degli stati KV scritti da alcune iterazioni da parte di iterazioni successive.
Variante di LSTM con memoria a matrice, usata come blocco ricorrente.

2611.19248.abs: Hybrid vision backbones interleave Mamba state-space mixers with self-attention, and a block's role is usually probed by removing it and measuring the damage. We test what that measurement means in MambaVision. On all 50,000 ImageNet validation images and three model sizes, every block ablation is paired with a size-matched null, the same perturbation with its channels shuffled or their signs flipped. In top-1 accuracy and in true-class rank, real and null damage are nearly indistinguishable in absolute terms: pooled over the blocks of MambaVision-T, the content effect lies within [-0.044,+0.016] percentage points (90% interval). Two attention-only controls show that the test detects content, with real ablations worse than their nulls by up to 4.2 points in DeiT-Small and 1.0 point in Swin-T. Part of MambaVision's near-equivalence reflects how little damage its blocks do (0.11--0.34 points on average, against 1.7 and 2.1). Scaled by damage, its content share is comparable to Swin-T's in accuracy, lower in rank, and far below DeiT-Small's: single-block damage in MambaVision is small and mostly positional. Ablation also hides what blocks carry together: removing all blocks of one type compounds damage to 3.7--8.4 times the sum of single effects, far more than size-matched nulls, including nulls that keep the alignment between the blocks' perturbations; for adjacent pairs, aligned nulls reproduce most of it. Freezing input-dependent selection in all Mamba mixers shows that it accounts for 20--32% of the Mamba contribution, mainly through the B and C projections. We turn these…

ov.problema: Nei backbone ibridi che alternano Mamba (state-space mixer) e self-attention, il ruolo di un blocco si sonda di solito rimuovendolo e misurando il danno. Non è chiaro cosa significhi davvero questa misura in MambaVision.
ov.idea: Gli autori confrontano ogni ablazione di blocco con un 'null' di pari dimensione: la stessa perturbazione con canali mescolati o segni invertiti. Così separano l'effetto del contenuto dall'effetto della semplice perturbazione. Usano anche controlli solo-attention e test su blocchi multipli.
ov.risultati: Su tutte le 50.000 immagini di validazione ImageNet e tre dimensioni, danno reale e null sono quasi indistinguibili in assoluto: effetto del contenuto in [-0.044,+0.016] punti percentuali (intervallo 90%). I controlli mostrano che il test rileva il contenuto: ablazioni reali peggiori dei null fino a 4.2 punti in DeiT-Small e 1.0 in Swin-T. Il danno dei blocchi di MambaVision è piccolo (0.11-0.34 punti contro 1.7 e 2.1).
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato: l'analisi sul congelamento della selezione input-dependent nei mixer Mamba non è riportata per intero.
