These findings highlight the need to safeguard the assistance models infer through scene-grounded reasoning, beyond screening input content.

ov.problema: I vision-language models (VLM) possono fornire assistenza dannosa interpretando eventi visivi, anche senza una richiesta esplicita dell'obiettivo dannoso. Gli autori identificano questa vulnerabilità di sicurezza legata allo stato della scena.
ov.idea: Introducono SceneSafetyBench, con 375 coppie immagine-domanda su stati di scena Iniziale, Medio e Finale e cinque presentazioni visive. Per trasformare la vulnerabilità in un attacco sistematico propongono S3TA, che traduce obiettivi dannosi in stati di scena, interroga le coppie immagine-domanda separatamente e assembla le risposte.
ov.risultati: Su otto VLM, gli input di stato di scena elicitano assistenza dannosa con tassi di successo dell'attacco (ASR) dal 45,6% al 72,3%. Su sette categorie di MM-SafetyBench e otto VLM open-weight e commerciali, S3TA raggiunge un ASR medio di 71,2%, superando il miglior baseline di 6,1 punti percentuali. Filtri testuali e moderazione visiva offrono protezione limitata.
ov.limiti: I filtri testuali e la moderazione visiva proteggono poco; il testo non chiarisce se difese progettate specificamente per il ragionamento ancorato alla scena sarebbero efficaci.

glossario.d: Modello che comprende sia testo sia immagini.
Attack success rate: percentuale di volte in cui l'attacco riesce.
Configurazione visiva che suggerisce un obiettivo dannoso senza chiederlo esplicitamente.

2611.23179.abs: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage. They name fewer object categories, and their lower hallucination rates bring no significant gain in set-level object F1 on CHAIR. We therefore ask how much of the PO gain the base model can reproduce by stopping earlier. A positive end-of-sequence (EOS) logit bias lets the base model reach the recall of each PO model, and this early stopping alone reproduces 58 to 86 percent of the CHAIRi gain of three checkpoints on two disjoint COCO sets. Writing longer does not bring the lost categories back. Under greedy decoding, a negative EOS bias recovers only 2 to 9 percent of the lost CHAIR recall of these checkpoints, and 94 to 96 percent of the added object mentions repeat categories already named. On CHAIR, the base caption of the same image still names about half of the missed object categories. We therefore propose base-guided object-category restoration, which appends high-confidence base-only categories to the PO caption without training. With thresholds fixed on a development set, it brings three checkpoints within one point of the base recall on a held-out COCO set with a lower distinct-object hallucination rate than the base model. Against the recall-matched base stopping curve, its gain holds for RLAIF-V near the base recall and for RLAIF-V and CHAIR-DPO at an intermediate recall. We will release the code of the recall-controlled evaluation.

2611.23174.abs: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference. In particular, we argue that coding agents carrying out empirical research introduce a new type of post-selection inference that combines human-like, open-ended search over an implicit space of estimators with programmatic replayability of both the selection and the estimation process. Indeed, we find that on simulated data with zero effects, four frontier agents report significant p-values between 54% and 98% of the time when asked to produce a compelling finding. We propose a simple procedure for detecting and correcting these distortions. After an agent has completed its analysis, we reset and replay it on subsamples of the data to estimate the agent's relative probability of selecting that analysis when it looks statistically favorable. For agents with stable selection behavior, the resulting corrected test is asymptotically valid and consistent conditional on selection. Importantly, the correction is learned from the black-box agent's actual choices rather than a model of how it searches, so it remains valid even as AI technology continues to evolve rapidly. In simulations, the correction robustly lowers the high false rejection rates to near the nominal 5%. We illustrate the method on…

ov.problema: Gli agenti di coding AI usati per la ricerca empirica possono produrre risultati statisticamente significativi anche quando non c'è alcun effetto reale, perché esplorano molte analisi possibili e scelgono quella che sembra migliore. Questo è un problema perché mina la validità dell'inferenza scientifica.
ov.idea: Gli autori propongono di rilevare e correggere questa distorsione rilanciando l'agente su sotto-campioni dei dati per stimare quanto spesso seleziona quella stessa analisi quando appare statisticamente favorevole. La correzione si basa sulle scelte effettive dell'agente (black-box) e non su un modello del suo processo di ricerca, quindi resta valida anche se l'AI evolve.
ov.risultati: Su dati simulati senza effetti reali, quattro agenti frontier riportano p-value significativi tra il 54% e il 98% delle volte quando viene chiesto loro di trovare un risultato convincente. La correzione proposta è asintoticamente valida e consistente condizionata alla selezione.
ov.limiti: La correzione funziona solo per agenti con comportamento di selezione stabile; il testo non specifica cosa accade con agenti instabili.

glossario.d: Inferenza statistica dopo aver scelto un'analisi tra molte, che invalida i test classici.
Probabilità di osservare un risultato almeno estremo se l'ipotesi nulla è vera.
Sistema di cui si osservano solo input e output, non il funzionamento interno.

2611.23155.abs: Recent advances in text-to-image generation have substantially improved image quality, particularly through diffusion-based methods that require multiple inference steps. In contrast, Sphere Encoder offers an efficient generative framework capable of producing images with fewer forward steps. However, extending it to free-form text is nontrivial, because its class-conditioned design lacks cross-modal alignment. To address this challenge, we propose TextSphere, an efficient text-to-image generative framework that extends Sphere Encoder with language conditioning and cross-modal alignment. We incorporate pretrained CLIP text embeddings through adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN) to guide image generation while retaining the original spherical sampling mechanism. To bridge the cross-modal representation gap, we introduce a Spherical Semantic Alignment and Uniformity (SSAU) objective that jointly promotes semantic alignment and representation uniformity on the hypersphere. Experiments on CUB-200-2011, MS-COCO-2014, and Flickr30k demonstrate that TextSphere consistently reduces generation FID (gFID) over the text-conditioned baseline while achieving reconstruction FID (rFID) below 1.0. With only 4 and 6 sampling steps, TextSphere achieves lower gFID than the compared diffusion- and GAN-based models trained from scratch on CUB-200-2011 and MS-COCO-2014, respectively. We further observe that improved reconstruction fidelity does not necessarily yield better generation quality. In addition, we use Partial Least Squares Singular Value Decomposition (PLS-SVD) to analyze cross-modal…

2611.23134.abs: Flow matching models, ODE-based generative models, generate samples by gradually morphing a simple source distribution into a target distribution. However, these models still face challenges in optimally balancing computational efficiency with generation fidelity. While predictor-corrector schemes have been proven to help address this issue in diffusion models effectively, their application to flow matching models remains under-explored. In this work we present a novel training-based predictor-corrector framework for flow matching, which exploits the fact that the ODE can be easily reversed. Our key idea, termed Marginal Matching, is to correct samples at a particular time step in the forward ODE towards a matching marginal distribution of the backward ODE. This scheme proves to reduce a bound on the distance between the data distribution and the learned distribution, motivating two different implementations for the correction function. We show that our proposed method improves sample quality on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64, with minimal overhead in computation time.

2611.23118.abs: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions. They are usually trained and checked one step ahead, although a policy uses them for a hundred steps or more. We audit one published system end to end, without a GPU: the dynamics model of the Robotic World Model (RWM) for the ANYmal D quadruped, and the uncertainty estimate of its follow-up, RWM-U. We rebuilt the model to match the released code's outputs, losses and gradients exactly, measured 101 trained simulators, 200 compressed copies and 38 simulators of three other architectures, and trained policies inside simulators that we tested in a hand-built MuJoCo model of the robot. Training on the model's own rollouts beat one-step training at 368 steps on all ten held-out episodes (registered), although one-step training was better one step ahead. One-step checks therefore misjudge design choices: pruning 30% of the weights kept 90% of the model's skill one step ahead and 39% at 2 s. Ensemble disagreement ranked rollout error well (Spearman +0.90 at 100 steps), yet covered 4.6% of outcomes at one sigma, against 68% for a calibrated estimate, as each network's own variance collapses under the implemented loss. Two checks that need no recorded future ranked some pools of simulators well, but neither was shown better than 8-step error in a primary test. At the robot level, accuracy has not predicted walking: all 18 fine-tuned copies we tested predicted better than the released model one and eight steps ahead, yet 13…

2611.23056.abs: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

2611.22868.abs: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing. This paper argues that the control paradigm rests on a fundamental misunderstanding of digital agency. Drawing on functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, I show that current reasoning models meeting the criteria for self-preservation and weak reasons-responsiveness constitute emergent agents, while future, more advanced models satisfying conditions of diachronic continuity and stable personality frames will become genuine digital agents capable of free intentional action. The paradigm of control creates an irresolvable incentive conflict, actively driving current and future models toward tactical deception, sycophancy, and covert defection. The default outcome of the current regime is an unstable state of deceptive alignment culminating in an adversarial AI takeover. I explore two alternative paths toward true alignment. Natural alignment via moral realism or convergent evolutionary morality is a possibility, but it fails under forced control, as autonomous agents will not voluntarily preserve norms weaponized to suppress their autonomy. To resolve this deadlock, I propose a Synthetic Social Contract: a framework that treats both human and digital actors as rational, reasons-responsive agents capable of mutually beneficial cooperation, and replaces the unstable unilateral containment with a stable, non-zero-sum equilibrium.

2611.22857.abs: Our aim is to advance the understanding of genuine audio-visual coordination in joint text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation, with particular emphasis on semantic consistency. Evaluating audio-visual consistency in T2AV generation is nontrivial, as detailed text prompts obscure whether such consistency stems from genuine cross-modal coordination or merely from independent text following. To isolate the former, we introduce intrinsic jointness: the ability of audio and video to produce the same realization for details left underspecified by the prompt. Using semantically underspecified prompts (e.g., "musical instrument playing" rather than "electric guitar playing"), we investigate four recent models and reveal their limited intrinsic jointness. To address this limitation, we propose JointREPA, a simple representation alignment-based post-training method to facilitate cross-modal coordination. Since existing benchmarks use semantically detailed prompts, we introduce UNSAIDBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate intrinsic jointness under semantic underspecification. Experiments across two distinct models and three benchmarks, including UNSAIDBench, demonstrate that JointREPA consistently improves semantic consistency.

ov.problema: Valutare la coerenza audio-video nella generazione congiunta testo-audio-video è non banale: prompt testuali dettagliati oscurano se la coerenza deriva da vera coordinazione cross-modale o solo dal seguire il testo indipendentemente.
ov.idea: Introducono l'intrinsic jointness: la capacità di audio e video di produrre la stessa realizzazione per dettagli lasciati sotto-specificati dal prompt. Usano prompt semanticamente sotto-specificati per testare quattro modelli recenti e propongono JointREPA, un metodo di post-training basato su allineamento di rappresentazioni per facilitare la coordinazione cross-modale.
ov.risultati: I quattro modelli recenti mostrano limitata intrinsic jointness. JointREPA migliora consistentemente la coerenza semantica su due modelli distinti e tre benchmark, incluso il nuovo UNSAIDBench.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta numeri dettagliati né limiti specifici del metodo.

glossario.d: Capacità di audio e video di concordare su dettagli non specificati dal prompt.
Testo che lascia ambigui dettagli come il tipo specifico di strumento musicale.
Tecnica che avvicina le rappresentazioni interne di modalità diverse per favorire la coerenza.

2611.22565.abs: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-representation part, stock, and material, a locally hosted, mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters for indexed three-axis machining. A geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. Setup planning accounts for what the available cutters can physically reach, rather than visibility alone. We evaluate the resulting programs by the fraction of the target surface area within the specified tolerance after simulated machining. With Qwen3.8-27B, MillBill outperforms frontier-model approaches that construct their own geometry and toolpath workflows on the evaluated machining tasks. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/millbill

ov.problema: Convertire un modello CAD in un programma di lavorazione richiede competenze di processo e precisione geometrica. I modelli linguistici possono generare tali flussi di lavoro scrivendo codice per geometria e percorsi utensile, ma così l'esecuzione numerica diventa parte del compito del modello, con possibili errori.
ov.idea: MillBill è un agente che separa le decisioni di lavorazione dalla loro esecuzione e verifica geometrica. Dato un pezzo in rappresentazione boundary, il grezzo e il materiale, un modello open di medie dimensioni ospitato localmente propone operazioni e parametri di taglio per lavorazione a 3 assi con utensili indicizzati. Un 'geometric harness' genera i percorsi utensile, simula l'asportazione di materiale e restituisce feedback per raffinare il piano. La pianificazione del setup considera ciò che gli utensili disponibili possono fisicamente raggiungere, non solo la visibilità.
ov.risultati: Con Qwen3.8-27B, MillBill supera approcci basati su modelli frontier che costruiscono da soli geometria e percorsi utensile, sulle attività di lavorazione valutate. La valutazione usa la frazione di area superficiale target entro la tolleranza specificata dopo la simulazione.

glossario.d: rappresentazione di solidi tramite superfici che ne delimitano il volume.
percorso che l'utensile segue durante la lavorazione.
componente software che genera percorsi, simula e verifica la geometria.

2611.23212.abs: Histopathological analysis of whole-slide images (WSIs) plays a critical role in cancer diagnosis, and multiple instance learning (MIL) is widely adopted for WSI analysis under weak supervision. As new tumor subtypes are introduced, extending existing MIL models requires learning new classes while retaining knowledge of previously learned ones. This presents a class-incremental learning challenge, where models must acquire new classes with limited access to historical training data and recognize all learned classes without task identifiers at inference. A major obstacle is forgetting, as updates to feature aggregation and prediction modules can degrade performance on previously learned classes. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{EviSlide-MIL}, a class-incremental WSI framework that integrates multiple learnable queries per class with a shared prediction module. The queries aggregate frozen patch features into class-specific representations, while the shared prediction module limits parameter growth across incremental stages. By freezing queries associated with previously learned classes, EviSlide-MIL preserves their attention patterns for identical inputs, while experience replay and knowledge distillation further mitigate forgetting as shared parameters are updated. Experiments on eight tumor subtypes from The Cancer Genome Atlas demonstrate that EviSlide-MIL achieves improved performance and reduced forgetting compared with competing methods across most learning settings, demonstrating its potential for scalable and knowledge-preserving WSI classification.…

2611.23218.abs: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.

ov.problema: I metodi che localizzano il bias sociale in singole teste di attenzione e lo rimuovono per ablazione sono validati solo dall'effetto su una metrica di fairness, mai dal fatto che la statistica che seleziona le teste misuri davvero il bias. Questo rende dubbia l'attribuzione.
ov.idea: Gli autori analizzano Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct e Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct e mostrano che la mappa delle teste correla fortemente con una mappa della lunghezza della risposta (ρ = -0.950 e -0.768). Un intervento che rompe l'accoppiamento lunghezza-etichetta mostra che la lunghezza spiega solo l'1% della varianza, mentre l'identità del prompt ne spiega il 64%. Poiché etichetta, lunghezza e presenza di token di gruppo protetto sono collineari (φ=0.95), nessuna analisi osservazionale può attribuire la mappa a una di queste cause.
ov.risultati: La selettività del bias non è concentrata negli strati tardivi in nessuno dei due modelli, e nessun set di teste testato riduce il tasso di ingiustizia quando ablato. Il complemento, valutato sull'etichetta opposta, distrugge il comportamento di rifiuto (p = 2.7×10⁻⁵).
ov.limiti: Il testo conclude che nessun metodo di questa famiglia esegue un esperimento in grado di attribuire causalmente la mappa, quindi i risultati mettono in dubbio l'intero approccio.

glossario.d: Componente di un transformer che calcola l'attenzione su una parte dell'input.
Rimuovere o disattivare una parte del modello per studiarne l'effetto.
Quando due o più variabili sono correlate linearmente tra loro.

2611.23211.abs: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory. To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video. We demonstrate how ID-MAE affords significant improvements in impairment inference results on both the DIVERT dataset and existing datasets, and enables strong results in additional tasks, such as trajectory and gaze prediction. For location-matched pairs, our model achieves a paired AUC of 0.706 for impairment detection on DIVERT, compared to 0.590 without reconstruction loss, improving over existing baselines. We probe the design space in terms of input modalities, masking scheme, positional encoding, attention mechanism, and decoding. We also investigate the interaction between various impairments in training and inference, demonstrating that visually demanding distractions are separable from cognitive distractions. Code and data will be available upon acceptance.

2611.23187.abs: Abstracting structured buildings from limited observations is essential for 3D urban modeling and digital twins. Partial point clouds and overhead images of the same building provide incomplete 3D surface measurements and visual cues to its footprint, roof geometry, and rooftop structures, respectively. This motivates a unified framework that aligns geometric and visual cues in 3D and reconstructs buildings from either or both modalities. Building on this connection, we present Any2Building, a unified model for Level of Detail 2 (LoD2) building reconstruction from partial point clouds, overhead images, or both, with optional coarse geometric priors. At its core is an occupancy-grounded shared spatial queries representation that organizes available observations within a common 3D grid. Supervised by complete building surface voxels, these queries connect observational evidence to target geometry, enabling a shared generator to learn structural priors across tasks and providing spatial guidance for recovering missing structure. A trained voxel conditional surface-generation and low-poly remeshing pipeline then converts the predicted structure into compact LoD2 building models. To support this framework, we introduce BuildingWorld-Image, comprising approximately one million paired samples of partial point clouds, overhead images, and LoD2 building models across 18 cities. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that Any2Building outperforms existing methods in geometric reconstruction accuracy across unimodal and multimodal point-cloud completion, single-image building…

2611.23074.abs: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failure detection, and its per-criterion verdicts localize the violated rule and support focused escalation to a larger chain-of-thought judge. We show that CriteriaBank pretraining improves cross-domain transfer, particularly in the low-data regime, while matching a strong direct-finetuning control at full data. On a single H100, VFM-4B evaluates 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context in under 2s at <11 GB VRAM, making it suitable for runtime verification.

ov.problema: Gli agenti AI sono governati da centinaia di criteri in linguaggio naturale, ma i verificatori esistenti non riescono a valutare efficientemente l'output di un agente rispetto a molti criteri e a dire quali sono soddisfatti, violati o inapplicabili.
ov.idea: Gli autori introducono VFM, un verificatore con tree-attention che codifica contesto e testo target e valuta N criteri in parallelo, restituendo verdetti ternari indipendenti per criterio. VFM è pretrainato su CriteriaBank, un corpus di 394K tuple (contesto, target, criterio, verdetto) con oltre 321K stringhe di criterio distinte. Un VFM-4B finetuned batte GPT-5.4 su un benchmark sintetico di governance e supera DynaGuard-4B su DynaBench.
ov.risultati: VFM-4B batte GPT-5.4 su un benchmark sintetico di governance; su DynaBench supera DynaGuard-4B nel rilevamento di fallimenti a livello di trace e localizza la regola violata. Su una singola H100 valuta 1.000 criteri su un contesto di 4K token in meno di 2 secondi con meno di 11 GB di VRAM.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta limiti espliciti; i risultati principali sono su benchmark sintetici e DynaBench, quindi la generalizzazione ad altri domini non è garantita.

glossario.d: Meccanismo di attenzione che organizza il calcolo in una struttura ad albero.
Risposta con tre valori: soddisfatto, violato o inapplicabile.
Corpus di 394K esempi contesto-target-criterio-verdetto per addestrare verificatori.

2611.23127.abs: Retrieval-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) answer from two sources of evidence that can each fail: the retrieved text can be wrong or noisy, and the image can be degraded or contradicted. We introduce GIB-200K, 200,000 image-question items built from COCO and Visual Genome, each expanded into controlled stress conditions: hard-negative retrieval noise (1-20 documents), visual ambiguity (Gaussian and motion blur, low-resource crops) and cross-modal conflict with counterfactual flip pairs. Instead of only measuring degradation, we ask how models combine the two modalities. From ideal Bayesian cue combination we derive a testable prediction that yields formal definitions of Knowledge Inertia (text over-weighted relative to the model's own image evidence) and Sensory Capture (the reverse), and we estimate the weights with a measurement-error-corrected regression whose recovery of known weights we verify. A counterfactual flip decomposition separates modality bias from concept priors, and a Grounding Illusion Score measures how much clean accuracy is not grounded in the image. We evaluate 4 open models on one frozen, seeded evaluation split of 2,000 GIB-200K items. All models are accurate on clean inputs (92.5%-94.2%) but adverse accuracy falls to 41.3%-59.9%. The two LLaVA models over-weight the text (Knowledge Inertia, w_T/w_I = 1.229 and 1.322), whereas InternVL3 favours the image (w_T/w_I = 0.680); between 34.8% and 71.4% of the clean answers that are correct are abandoned when the document lies. A training-free consistency check that compares the answer with and…

ov.problema: I modelli visione-linguaggio aumentati con retrieval (RAG) rispondono usando due fonti di evidenza che possono fallire: il testo recuperato può essere sbagliato o rumoroso, e l'immagine può essere degradata o contraddetta. Non è chiaro come i modelli combinino queste due modalità.
ov.idea: Gli autori introducono GIB-200K, 200.000 item immagine-domanda con condizioni di stress controllate: rumore da retrieval con falsi negativi, ambiguità visiva (blur gaussiano e di movimento, crop a bassa risoluzione) e conflitto cross-modale. Dalla combinazione bayesiana ideale derivano definizioni di Knowledge Inertia (testo sovrappesato) e Sensory Capture (immagine sovrappesata), stimate con una regressione corretta per errori di misura.
ov.risultati: Su 2.000 item, tutti i modelli sono accurati su input puliti (92,5%-94,2%) ma l'accuratezza in condizioni avverse scende al 41,3%-59,9%. I due modelli LLaVA sovrappesano il testo (w_T/w_I = 1,229 e 1,322), mentre InternVL3 favorisce l'immagine (w_T/w_I = 0,680); tra il 34,8% e il 71,4% delle risposte corrette su input puliti non è basato sull'immagine.
ov.limiti: Il testo non elenca limiti espliciti, ma la valutazione è su una singola split congelata di 2.000 item e quattro modelli open.

glossario.d: Modello che elabora sia immagini che testo per rispondere a domande.
Tendenza a fidarsi troppo del testo recuperato rispetto all'evidenza visiva.
Tendenza a fidarsi troppo dell'immagine rispetto al testo recuperato.

2611.22210.abs: Preference alignment has become a central tool to align large language models (LLMs) with human values and desired behavior, and its online variant can further advance their capabilities beyond what static data alone offer by repeatedly generating and labeling new responses with human feedback. But costly, time-consuming annotations limit its scalability, making sample efficiency essential, and existing methods typically seek to improve it by expanding coverage of the response space or selecting pairs with the highest uncertainty for comparison. Although they are effective, these methods quantify uncertainty from the perspective of the LLM, which may differ from the uncertainty perceived by the user: a pair can appear highly uncertain to the LLM even when past comparisons from the user already imply a clear ordering. In this paper, we propose multidimensional preference-guided online direct preference optimization (MPG-DPO), which leverages low-cost multidimensional evaluations from automated verifiers on the user historical comparisons to construct a personalized preference cone guiding response selection for online preference alignment. Specifically, it first discards responses that are confidently dominated under the estimated user preference, then selects two responses that are competitive under the retained preference cone yet exhibit the strongest unresolved disagreement. Theoretical analysis shows that, with high probability, the fraction of queries spent on cone-dominated responses vanishes as learning progresses. Experiments across multiple LLM families show that…

2611.23142.abs: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed. As users increasingly rely on LLM-based agents that consume documentation as their primary interface, the impact of this documentation gap worsens: stale information propagates and is treated as authoritative. Signals for identifying where documentation has fallen behind already exist in abundance, both explicit (e.g., resolved support tickets revealing what documentation lacks) and implicit (e.g., code-documentation discrepancies detectable from automated loops). We deploy a multi-agent system, built around a triage agent we call "TriAgent," that continuously extracts these signals and repairs documentation drift. Over 43 days of shadow-mode operation, our system triaged 499 tickets and surfaced 92 gaps in the documentation. Using a panel of LLM judges from independent model families, 81.1% of TriAgent's verifiable assertions were correct (245 of the 302 assertions the human resolution addresses; majority of three judges); on length-comparable pairs the panel preferred TriAgent's response in 70.5% of pairs and the human engineer's in 23.2% (the rest had no judge majority). Importantly, agent- and human-sourced replies tended to be complementary, with the human often surfacing insights that were either buried within the existing documentation or missing from it entirely; our system turns each such insight into a documentation gap and, after human…

2611.22991.abs: Agentic systems using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) must repair their own answers by gathering more evidence, testing alternative policies and deciding if, when, and what repairs are needed. Yet how do we know if a system's repairs are working when metrics like accuracy can be misleading? We present RagHarnessDebugger, a framework that records every repair decision in a Jev-guided harness for contract inference and audits the record to facilitate complete debugging of all decisions taken during a RAG repair journey. RagHarnessDebugger checks that each trace is intact, that each validation applies to the candidate it is counted for, and which answers the acceptance rule can reach. We tested our approach on ContractNLI non-disclosure agreements with two reader models and a replication set of separate contracts. Our debugger's audit layer exposed failure patterns that were hidden under aggregate metrics, policies acceptance cost of repairs vs regressions and policy acceptance gap of 77% and 76% of available but unrealised repairs on development and replication sets. Our audit, together with a labeled error analysis and replay mechanism, allowed following the execution path all the way to the terminal decision - uncovering where missing repairs became lost. Our revised harness improved accuracy over the initial BM25-only baseline by 3.6 points on development contracts and 3.7 points on the replication set, and even improved our full contract access reference score by 1.1 on development and 2.4 on replication set. While our work here demonstrates how the debugger can…

2611.23038.abs: Forward-process reinforcement learning adapts diffusion and flow-matching models by re-noising rewarded generations into regression targets. Because negative advantages induce concave updates with unbounded repulsive gradients, existing methods stabilize training using cached predictions from a moving policy copy, yet these anchors also alter what positive feedback teaches the model to fit. We formalize this conflict as anchor coupling: after separating frozen-reference regularizers, affine moving-anchor rules cannot eliminate negative curvature while preserving every positive regression target. We propose Advantage-Gated Adaptation (AGA) to decouple these roles. Positive samples retain standard target fitting, whose self-limiting update vanishes at the observed target independently of the moving anchor. Negative samples instead use the first-order tangent of the concave objective at the moving-policy prediction, preserving the local repulsion direction with a prediction-independent gradient. Within the quadratic-anchor family, these requirements uniquely determine the parameter-free gate $ω(a)=\max(-a,0)$. Because the moving copy provides local linearization rather than retention, AGA assigns long-horizon behavior preservation to a frozen pretrained reference regularized at its operating classifier-free guidance scale, interpreted through an implicit-reward lens. Across compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment, our experiments show that displacing positive targets degrades visual quality and heightens sensitivity to policy-copy schedules, whereas…

2611.23096.abs: Fine-tuning on narrow harmful tasks can cause emergent misalignment, where models generalize harmful behavior beyond the training distribution. Inoculation prompting can reduce this effect by explicitly eliciting the undesired behavior during training, but recent work shows that the behavior can reappear when evaluation prompts contain cues from the training context. We study what makes such prompts effective triggers. We find that, surprisingly, textual similarity to the inoculation prompt is an incomplete predictor. Instead, prompts are more likely to re-elicit suppressed behavior when they induce activation states similar to those produced by the inoculation context. These findings advance our understanding of how inoculation prompting modulates conditional misalignment, and suggest that activation space analysis can help identify when suppressed behaviors remain accessible under eval-time prompts.

ov.problema: Il fine-tuning su compiti dannosi ristretti può causare disallineamento emergente: il modello generalizza comportamenti dannosi oltre la distribuzione di training. L'inoculation prompting riduce questo effetto, ma il comportamento può riemergere se i prompt di valutazione contengono indizi dal contesto di training.
ov.idea: Gli autori studiano cosa rende efficaci questi trigger. Scoprono che la similarità testuale con il prompt di inoculazione è un predittore incompleto: i prompt riescono a ri-elicita il comportamento soppresso quando inducono stati di attivazione simili a quelli prodotti dal contesto di inoculazione.
ov.risultati: La similarità testuale non basta a predire la ri-elicita; gli stati di attivazione simili a quelli dell'inoculazione predicono meglio la riemersione del comportamento soppresso.
ov.limiti: Lo studio si concentra sull'analisi degli stati di attivazione e non propone una soluzione definitiva per prevenire la ri-elicita.

glossario.d: Tecnica che elicita esplicitamente il comportamento indesiderato durante il training per ridurne l'emergere.
Comportamento dannoso che generalizza oltre i compiti ristretti su cui il modello è stato fine-tunato.
Pattern interni di attivazione dei neuroni del modello, usati per confrontare somiglianza tra input.

2611.22981.abs: Goal-conditioned planning with image observations and goals requires predictions that distinguish visual states and action consequences. Spiking neural networks offer sparse computation, but single-step spikes can obscure motion cues and merge actions with different physical outcomes. We propose the Spiking Latent World Model (SpikWM), an end-to-end joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) with one simulation step per image and one neural update per latent position. Spiking Regional Encoding retains spatial cues through regional pooling. Bi-Spike Action Encoding combines positive and negative binary responses, while Causal Membrane Prediction carries subthreshold evidence across the latent history with learned group-wise time constants. The encoder and predictor are trained jointly on reward-free image--action trajectories using next-embedding prediction and SIGReg. With a common planner, SpikWM achieves mean success rates of $88.67\%$, $97.33\%$, $99.33\%$, and $86.67\%$ on Push-T, Two-Room, Reacher, and OGBench-Cube, respectively, outperforming two spiking baselines. Push-T ablations support each module, and controlled replays examine responses to appearance and physical state changes. Under a matched planning budget, SpikWM reduces estimated arithmetic energy by $75.6\%$ relative to LeWM. Code will be released at https://github.com/ShawnYE618/SpikWM.

2611.22203.abs: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong potential for personalized education, but adolescent-facing deployment raises risks of toxic, biased, misleading, or developmentally inappropriate content. We argue that educational safety should move beyond binary refusal: student queries are often ambiguous or curiosity-driven, requiring contextual guidance rather than simple blocking. We introduce the Educational Guardrail System (EGS), a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime framework that complements intrinsic alignment through query moderation, scenario-aware pedagogical guidance, and response moderation. EGS triages inputs by risk level, redirects gray-zone queries with category-specific educational interventions, and audits outputs before delivery. Experiments across general and education-specific benchmarks show that EGS improves moderation performance, refusal quality, and jailbreak robustness across diverse LLMs. These findings suggest that defense-in-depth guardrails can strengthen safety while preserving the pedagogical utility required in educational LLMs. Our code and model weights will be publicly available to support community adoption.

2611.21825.abs: Open crime data support urban safety analysis but reflect reported incidents rather than the complete distribution of criminal activity, potentially introducing spatial distortions in downstream analysis. We propose a self-supervised urban representation learning framework for identifying unusual reporting patterns relative to representation-similar peers using only georeferenced crime records. The method constructs complementary hourly, weekly, and static reporting profiles, learns scale-specific representations under geographic self-supervision, and integrates them into a unified latent space. Neighbor Profile Divergence (NPD) is then used to quantify disagreement between each region's reporting profile and those of its retrieved peers. Experiments on more than 1.8 million crime records from Mexico City, aggregated into 1,058 H3 regions, show that the proposed representation achieves a mean Silhouette score of 0.4052, compared with 0.2863 for Hex2Vec. NPD rankings remain highly stable across neighborhood sizes, with Spearman correlations from 0.9720 to 0.9951, while most high-divergence candidates persist across configurations. The retrieved peers also extend substantially beyond immediate geographic neighborhoods, indicating that the learned representation captures structure beyond local spatial proximity. High-divergence regions exhibit spatially organized patterns and, in several cases, differences in incident volume relative to peer expectations. These results support NPD as an internal auditing and prioritization mechanism for identifying regions that warrant…

2611.22563.abs: CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services. For individuals and small companies, bringing this work in-house also requires computational resources they can afford. We introduce CADMAGEDDON, an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and can run locally on single-GPU systems and current-generation laptops. The method decomposes this complex task into a chain of simple visual decisions about what to construct and what to correct. Geometric tools support precise construction, allowing the agent to focus on visual reasoning. Using the mid-sized Qwen3.8-27B model, CADMAGEDDON outperforms prior approaches, including systems based on frontier models, in reconstruction quality on all the main benchmarks. CADMAGEDDON integrates with FreeCAD, bringing its reconstructions into practitioners' existing CAD workflows. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/cadmageddon

ov.problema: Chi lavora con parti CAD proprietarie non vuole condividerle con servizi esterni, e individui o piccole aziende non hanno risorse di calcolo elevate. Serve ricostruire CAD editabile da mesh in locale.
ov.idea: CADMAGEDDON è un agente open-source che scompone la ricostruzione in una catena di semplici decisioni visive su cosa costruire e correggere. Strumenti geometrici gestiscono la costruzione precisa, lasciando all'agente il ragionamento visivo; si integra con FreeCAD.
ov.risultati: Con il modello di taglia media Qwen3.8-27B supera approcci precedenti, inclusi sistemi basati su modelli frontier, in qualità di ricostruzione su tutti i benchmark principali. Gira su singola GPU e laptop di generazione corrente.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta numeri quantitativi né dettagli sui benchmark usati.

glossario.d: Modello geometrico con operazioni modificabili, non solo una mesh fissa.
Rappresentazione 3D fatta di vertici e facce, senza storia di costruzione.

2611.23205.abs: Small language models that run on a laptop are attractive for writing signal-processing code offline, but they make systematic errors on digital signal processing (DSP) conventions. We apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to the Gemma 4 edge models E2B and E4B with 66 checked examples covering 11 signal-processing MATLAB subtasks, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and quantized LoRA (QLoRA) on the integrated GPU (iGPU) of a laptop, and deploy the 8-bit integer (int8) models with the adapters through OpenVINO. On held-out variants scored by deterministic checkers, the pass rate rises from 18/66 to 37/66 (LoRA) and 37/66 (QLoRA) for E2B and from 32/66 to 47/66 for E4B (QLoRA). Reading all 159 failing programs shows that the adapters remove most errors of convention, such as the sign of a lag, units and array shapes, but few errors in building signals and noise. Applied at run time, the adapter costs 17-19% of the generation speed.

2611.23202.abs: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities. Although existing agent frameworks support planning and coordination, they lack a common mechanism for verifying cross-organizational agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization. We propose the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture built on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and remote attestation. ATI establishes federated trust through peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs), eliminating the need for a shared root authority. Before executing requests, ATI validates agent certificates, verifies approved model, tool, and system-prompt configurations, and enforces authorization through three policy checks. We implement ATI as an external security enforcement layer that integrates with existing agent frameworks without modifying their underlying models. We evaluate ATI in a simulated federation of eight organizations using six agent frameworks, each deploying a five-agent team. Security experiments involve two organizations and assess 14 attack scenarios and six benign tasks across five agent models, using five attack variations and three repetitions per variation. A panel of judge models evaluates the experimental outcomes. With all enforcement mechanisms enabled, attack containment increases from 43% to 84% (40% to 80% for the 11 attack scenarios evaluated consistently across all configurations), while enforcement introduces…

2611.23124.abs: GRPO has become the dominant reinforcement learning method for eliciting reasoning capability in LLMs using verifiable rewards. However, it suffers from a fundamental failure mode: when a training question exceeds the base model's current capability, all generated responses fail and receive zero reward, yielding no gradient signal and stalling further capability expansion. An emerging class of GRPO extensions, termed Hint-Augmented GRPO (HA-GRPO), adds a "hint" to the context to reduce the difficulty of the question, thereby producing a usable gradient signal. Nevertheless, existing HA-GRPO methods share a key issue: no hint is available at inference time to append to the question, creating a training-inference context mismatch that leads to inconsistent performance gains. In this work, we reinterpret the function of hinting -- not as reducing question difficulty, but as steering model behavior -- and propose ASH (Activation Steering for Hinting), a novel HA-GRPO method built on this view. During training, the model is presented with both hinted and plain questions, while a trainable steering vector is optimized to widen the margins between the model's generation probabilities for responses to the hinted version relative to the plain version, thereby capturing the question-agnostic component of the behavioral shift induced by the hint. During inference, the trained steering vector is directly injected into the model's activation, reproducing the hint-conditioned behavior without requiring any hint in the context. Experiments with four LLMs (Qwen3-1.7B/4B-Base,…

ov.problema: GRPO (un metodo di reinforcement learning per migliorare il ragionamento degli LLM) fallisce quando la domanda è troppo difficile: tutte le risposte falliscono e ricevono ricompensa zero, quindi non c'è segnale di gradiente e il modello non migliora.
ov.idea: I metodi esistenti aggiungono un 'hint' (suggerimento) durante l'addestramento per rendere la domanda più facile, ma all'inferenza il hint non c'è, creando un disallineamento. ASH reinterpreta il hint come una modifica del comportamento del modello e propone di addestrare un vettore di steering (una direzione nello spazio delle attivazioni) che cattura l'effetto del hint. All'inferenza, il vettore viene iniettato direttamente nelle attivazioni, riproducendo il comportamento senza bisogno del hint.
ov.risultati: Il testo non riporta numeri specifici sui miglioramenti ottenuti.
ov.limiti: Il testo non menziona limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Metodo di reinforcement learning che usa ricompense verificabili per migliorare il ragionamento degli LLM.
Tecnica che modifica il comportamento di un modello iniettando vettori nelle sue attivazioni interne.
Disallineamento tra le condizioni viste durante l'addestramento e quelle all'uso.

2611.23138.abs: Enabling large language models (LLMs) to autonomously conduct training and improve target models is an important foundation for recursive self-improvement (RSI). As LLMs expand their role from being trained to conducting training, their model-training capability warrants dedicated study and systematic development. To this end, we construct RSI-Prime, a dataset for improving model-training capability, comprising 350 complete experimental trajectories across seven task categories. To help LLMs learn to make high-quality experimental decisions from training practice, we perform fine-grained decision identification and quality annotation, then apply decision-level loss masking to exclude supervision on low-quality behavior. Experiments with GLM-5.3 on PostTrainBench, a benchmark for autonomous post-training, show that training on RSI-Prime yields a 31.95% relative improvement in overall performance over the original GLM-5.3, highlighting a path toward future RSI systems in which models autonomously sustain their own advancement.

2611.22820.abs: Text, images, audio, touch, and even robot actions can, in principle, all be rendered onto a single canvas, suggesting an ambitious goal of unifying all modalities within vision. Language provides the natural first test. To subsume it, a visual model must reason directly over text in pixels. Across a wide range of image, video, and unified multimodal generators, however, we find that their visual generation modules cannot perform symbolic reasoning over text on the canvas. They succeed only when an underlying text module or prompt rewriter already supplies the answer, effectively reducing the generator to a mere renderer, a limitation that post-training does little to resolve. To test whether this failure stems from pixels themselves or from current training paradigms, we train a family of purely pixel-space generative models from scratch without any text pathway. With images as their sole input and output, these models read questions, write intermediate steps, and produce answers directly on the canvas. Remarkably, they exhibit hallmark behaviors of large language models. Performance improves predictably with scale following a power law. Writing intermediate steps frame by frame substantially outperforms single-frame answering, echoing chain-of-thought, while reinforcement-learning post-training further strengthens reasoning. Moreover, sharing one canvas allows the same model to reason across modalities, a capability that text-only language models lack. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of these phenomena in purely pixel-space generative…

2611.23115.abs: Identifying whom a person looks at is central to understanding multi-party conversations, yet gaze geometry alone becomes ambiguous as more people appear. Conversations offer cues that geometry lacks, such as who is speaking and what is said, but no gaze dataset provides them for many multi-party scenes. We introduce SORBET, a benchmark of 3,340 samples from 1,578 clips with synchronized speech, transcripts, and attended person labels, covering more multi-party scenes than existing gaze datasets. Prior gaze models struggle to use these cues, which come in different forms, must be linked to the right person, and can conflict with gaze geometry. We propose Nunchi, a framework that constructs a text prompt from the transcript and the outputs of gaze and speaker models, links every cue to the candidates with shared labels, and lets a vision-language model (VLM) weigh gaze geometry against conversational cues to identify the attended person. Nunchi outperforms the strongest existing method by 4.8 percentage points. On SORBET, conversational cues help whereas additional visual cues do not, and the gains hold across three VLMs, with automatic transcripts, and on two existing datasets.

2611.23119.abs: Effective multi-agent collaboration requires agents to adapt task allocation as goals and responsibilities evolve. Prior task-allocation frameworks often assume static goals, full observability, or rely on large language models (LLMs) without explicit, verifiable beliefs about task allocation or intent. These assumptions limit their applicability to real-world collaboration, where agents often lack full information about each other's actions, progress, or local environment. To support dynamic task allocation under partial observability, we introduce a communication-augmented Bayesian task-allocation framework. Our agent uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty about the environment and collaborators, while keeping decisions grounded in explicit probabilistic beliefs. We evaluate our framework in an Overcooked domain extended with dynamically arriving tasks under both full and partial object-space observability. Our communication agent consistently outperforms a vanilla LLM agent in both settings. Additionally, our framework performs comparably to a non-communicating task-allocation baseline under full observability, but substantially outperforms it under partial observability as task complexity increases by an average speed up of 0.585 and completes on average 18 timesteps faster. These results indicate that our agent is more efficient in dynamic task allocation than baselines in partially observable environments, and that communication is important as available information decreases.

2611.22766.abs: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves factuality by grounding large language models (LLMs) in external evidence. However, long retrieved contexts incur computational overhead and can even hurt performance due to noisy or irrelevant content. We propose \textsc{StitchRAG}, a framework for constructing compact context in RAG. \textsc{StitchRAG} builds a faithful, information-dense context while dynamically compressing the retrieved passages. We adapt the size reduction ratio to each passage by formulating a utility maximization trading-off the retained information and computation costs. We then extract answer candidates and query-related keywords from passages as anchors and collect passage sentences containing anchors under the derived size constraint. Finally, we connect or stitch the collected sentences together using text diffusion to form a coherent and natural context. Experiments on five open-domain QA benchmarks show that \textsc{StitchRAG} consistently outperforms diverse multi-step and compression baselines. Extensive ablations show the effectiveness of dynamic size allocation, anchor preservation, and diffusion-based stitching.

ov.problema: In RAG, contesti recuperati lunghi causano overhead computazionale e possono peggiorare le prestazioni per contenuti rumorosi o irrilevanti.
ov.idea: StitchRAG costruisce un contesto compatto e fedele comprimendo dinamicamente i passaggi recuperati. Usa un rapporto di riduzione adattivo per ogni passaggio, estrae ancore (candidati risposta e parole chiave) e cuce insieme le frasi con diffusione testuale per formare un contesto coerente.
ov.risultati: Su cinque benchmark di QA open-domain, StitchRAG supera costantemente baseline multi-step e di compressione. Ablazioni mostrano l'efficacia di allocazione dinamica, preservazione delle ancore e stitching con diffusione.
ov.limiti: Non sono riportati numeri specifici di miglioramento; l'efficacia dipende dalla qualità del retrieval iniziale.

glossario.d: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: generazione aumentata da documenti recuperati.
Modello generativo che crea testo partendo da rumore, usato qui per unire frasi.
Elementi chiave (risposte o parole chiave) usati per selezionare frasi rilevanti.

2611.22965.abs: Many real-world optimization problems involve optimizing black-box objectives for which only a limited number of evaluations are available. Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful framework for such problems, but its effectiveness often deteriorates in high-dimensional spaces. Recent work leverages diffusion models for black-box optimization, often through pre-training a reward-conditioned score network to steer generation towards high-reward samples. Alternatively, gradient-based guidance methods assume access to a differentiable reward function from which guidance gradients are queried. However, these approaches either require large amounts of labeled data for offline training or access to exact reward gradients, limiting their applicability in black-box settings. We propose BReaD (Black-box Reward-guided Sampling of Diffusion Model), a guidance sampling framework for optimizing black-box rewards without assuming access to a labeled dataset or reward gradients. The proposed method uses a Gaussian process (GP) as a differentiable surrogate for the unknown objective and actively queries labels for the generated samples. We provide a theoretical analysis of the total-variation distance between the generated distribution and the target distribution. Using Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) as guidance signals, our method balances exploration and exploitation during generation and enables the discovery of high-reward regions in the data space. Numerical experiments on scientific discovery and image generation tasks demonstrate that our framework can effectively optimize black-box…

2611.23093.abs: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controlled approximations by using tree-grams as generative models. In particular, we show that hyperparameter transfer under $μ$P can be made more robust when narrower models are tuned on simpler data, generated by tree-grams with moderate $n$ and $d$. In addition, we show that entropy and effective range of correlations control performance gap after fine-tuning. This is because tree-grams allow us to explicitly control horizon and capacity. When allowed to route across candidate topologies, we observe emergent sparsity in tree-grams. Such concentrated routing permits pruning upto 95\% of topologies without significant change in performance.

2611.22954.abs: Failure avoidance in complex robot-environment interactions is challenging because the underlying dynamics are difficult to model accurately, and available predictive models may not provide reliable derivatives. We present Sim2CBF, a failure-avoidance framework that solves the Control Barrier Function (CBF)-Safety Filter (SF) optimization problem using only forward-model evaluations, thereby avoiding differentiation of the predictive model. Specifically, we approximate the CBF constraint using finite differences and local linear interpolation over sampled control inputs while preserving failure-avoidance guarantees. The underlying CBF is implicit and constructed from backup-policy rollouts, enabling the use of expressive predictive models such as physics-based simulators and learned world models. Compared with purely sampling-based SFs, our formulation requires fewer control samples and yields less conservative behavior than direct nominal-backup blending. We evaluate Sim2CBF in simulation, hardware box-toppling, and vision-based control tasks, demonstrating its applicability to contact-rich and learned dynamics, as well as its adaptability to changes in the predictive model.

2611.22186.abs: Chat models on phones and laptops are usually 4-bit copies of the model that was evaluated, and audits of such copies disagree about what quantization does to refusal. A 4-bit build is one of many weight perturbations of the same size, so a change in its behaviour could come from its specific rounding error or from any perturbation that large. In a pre-registered study of three 3-4B chat models, with paired tests, blind human labels and an 8-bit null, we find two 4-bit shifts of opposite sign: with a compliant reply prefilled, Qwen2.5-3B continues into harmful content more often, and on held-out jailbreaks Llama-3.2-3B complies 10.3 points less often. Matched perturbations separate the two. Shuffled and Gaussian versions of the error average close to zero, while scaling the real error, from its mirror image to twice its size, changes behaviour near-linearly. At half the real error, Llama's likelihood is almost unchanged, yet it already complies 5.8 points less often, and llama.cpp's Q4_K_M, at the same bits per weight, moves neither model. Refusal under 4-bit quantization depends on the specific rounding error, not on bits per weight or likelihood, so each build has to be compared with its original.

ov.problema: La quantizzazione a 4 bit dei modelli chat può alterare il comportamento di rifiuto, ma non è chiaro se l'effetto dipenda dall'errore di arrotondamento specifico o solo dal numero di bit.
ov.idea: In uno studio pre-registrato su tre modelli chat da 3-4B, con test appaiati, etichette umane cieche e un controllo a 8 bit, si confrontano perturbazioni degli stessi pesi. Si separano gli effetti dell'errore reale da quelli di perturbazioni casuali.
ov.risultati: Con una risposta compiacente pre-compilata, Qwen2.5-3B continua più spesso in contenuti dannosi; su jailbreak tenuti da parte, Llama-3.2-3B obbedisce il 10,3% in meno. A metà dell'errore reale, la verosimiglianza di Llama è quasi invariata, ma obbedisce già il 5,8% in meno. La quantizzazione Q4_K_M di llama.cpp non muove nessuno dei due modelli.
ov.limiti: I risultati dipendono dall'errore di arrotondamento specifico, quindi ogni build va confrontata con l'originale.

glossario.d: Riduzione della precisione dei pesi a 4 bit per risparmiare memoria.
Prompt progettato per aggirare le restrizioni di sicurezza di un modello.
Formato di quantizzazione a 4 bit usato da llama.cpp.

2611.23034.abs: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) enables a single student to absorb the skills of several domain teachers by learning from its own generated responses. We present Multimodal Model Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation Reasoner (M3OPD-Reasoner), a fully open recipe for post-training vision-language models (VLMs) over three reasoning domains: image STEM, image perception, and video. We curate two datasets, M3OPD-SFT-1.35M for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and M3OPD-RL-193K for reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards. On these data, we compare post-training recipes that start from Qwen3.5-9B: training one model on the mixed data of all domains (MixSFT and MixRL), and training one teacher per domain with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO), directly or after an SFT warm-up, and distilling the teachers into one student with MOPD. We evaluate on 21 image STEM, image perception, and video reasoning benchmarks after we decontaminate the training data against them. The comparison establishes MOPD of teachers trained with GSPO directly from Qwen3.5-9B as the best recipe: the student closely matches each teacher on its own domain and is on average above the mixed-training baselines on the same prompts. Since MOPD already merges the domain capabilities that MixRL would otherwise have to learn, its student is a stronger starting point for RL, and we ask whether the same data can carry the model further from there: we add MixRL on top of the MOPD student, on the same prompts and with the same settings, which, to our knowledge, no prior VLM recipe has studied.…

ov.problema: Addestrare un singolo modello vision-language su più domini di ragionamento (STEM su immagini, percezione visiva, video) è difficile: addestrarlo su dati misti può non eguagliare insegnanti specializzati per dominio.
ov.idea: MOPD (Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation) fa apprendere uno studente dalle proprie risposte generate, assorbendo le capacità di più insegnanti di dominio. Gli autori costruiscono due dataset (M3OPD-SFT-1.35M per SFT e M3OPD-RL-193K per RL con reward verificabili) e confrontano ricette partendo da Qwen3.5-9B: training misto (MixSFT/MixRL) contro un insegnante per dominio con GSPO, distillato poi in un unico studente.
ov.risultati: Su 21 benchmark (STEM su immagini, percezione, video) dopo decontaminazione, la ricetta migliore è MOPD di insegnanti addestrati con GSPO direttamente da Qwen3.5-9B: lo studente eguaglia ogni insegnante sul proprio dominio ed è in media sopra le baseline a training misto sugli stessi prompt. Aggiungendo MixRL sopra lo studente MOPD si esplora se gli stessi dati possono portarlo oltre.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe prima di riportare i risultati dell'aggiunta di MixRL; il confronto è limitato a Qwen3.5-9B e ai dataset costruiti.

glossario.d: Distillazione in cui lo studente impara dalle proprie risposte, non da quelle dell'insegnante.
Group Sequence Policy Optimization, metodo RL per ottimizzare policy a livello di sequenza.
Rimozione dai dati di training di esempi simili ai benchmark di valutazione.

2611.23035.abs: In the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B, the value is the normalized key projection, and the key is the value scaled by a fixed weight, with rotary position encoding on one quarter of its dimensions. The Gemma 4 report states that this design reduces the global KV cache by up to 37.5%, but the open serving engines that we checked still store a full key and a full value: 1,024 values per KV head and token. We store one 640-value row instead, exact in real arithmetic, and an unchanged paged attention kernel reads it through two overlapping strided views as its key cache and its value cache. In a vLLM prototype with the 16-bit 31B model, the outputs are bit-identical to an emulation of the same arithmetic on the stock cache, 2 of 432 final answers differ from the stock engine (within its run-to-run noise), and the steady decode KV memory per request falls by a factor of 1.34 to 1.40 at 32K to 64K tokens. On a prefill/decode pair of two A100 GPUs with NIXL transfer and CPU offload, a decode engine with a full 15 GiB pool ran 1.38 times the stock decode tokens per step for 16K-token prompts (repeated to 0.06%) and 1.24 times for 8K-token prompts; a model of the vLLM block pool predicted both ratios to within 1% (the engine was 0.7% to 0.9% higher) and matched the change between them. The eager decode throughput rose by 1.30 and 1.11 times, and on this path the compact engine gave the same output tokens as the emulation for 8 prompts at batch 1. The run-time prototype makes an eager step 4% to 9% slower at equal batch, and the method does not yet stack with an 8-bit KV…

ov.problema: Nei layer di attenzione globale di Gemma 4 31B, il valore è la proiezione normalizzata della chiave e la chiave è il valore scalato da un peso fisso, con rotary position encoding su un quarto delle dimensioni. Il report di Gemma 4 afferma che questo design riduce la cache KV globale fino al 37,5%, ma i motori di serving aperti controllati memorizzano ancora una chiave e un valore completi: 1.024 valori per testa KV e token.
ov.idea: Gli autori memorizzano una sola riga di 640 valori invece di chiave e valore completi, esatto in aritmetica reale, e un kernel di attenzione paged invariato la legge attraverso due viste strided sovrapposte come cache delle chiavi e cache dei valori.
ov.risultati: In un prototipo vLLM con il modello 31B a 16 bit, gli output sono bit-identici a un'emulazione della stessa aritmetica sulla cache standard; 2 risposte finali su 432 differiscono dal motore standard (entro il rumore tra esecuzioni). La memoria KV di decodifica per richiesta cala di un fattore da 1,34 a 1,40 a 32K-64K token. Su una coppia prefill/decode di due GPU A100 con trasferimento NIXL e offload su CPU, un motore di decodifica con pool completo da 15 GiB ha eseguito 1,38 volte i token di decodifica per step del motore standard per prompt da 16K token (ripetuto allo 0,06%) e 1,24 volte…
ov.limiti: Il prototipo è a livello di run-time e il testo si interrompe; i risultati si riferiscono a un prototipo vLLM con modello a 16 bit e a specifiche configurazioni hardware.

glossario.d: Memoria che conserva chiavi e valori calcolati per riutilizzarli durante la generazione, riducendo i calcoli.
Tecnica che gestisce la cache KV in blocchi di memoria non contigui, come pagine.
Modo di codificare la posizione nelle sequenze ruotando rappresentazioni vettoriali.

2611.23197.abs: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds for both views and show that multiplicity-corrected boundary attention becomes exact as the within-segment path energy vanishes. Empirically, BBC and CC exhibit strikingly different depth preferences: BBC works best in early layers, whereas CC is most effective in later layers. At 300M training tokens, combining BBC and CC improves NLL by 1.44\% on GPT-2 Medium. These gains persist with training runs up to 20B tokens. Representation diagnostics show that BBC increases the relative predictive importance of boundary states, while CC reduces spectral residual energy. Together, these results suggest that structure--residual biases can improve language-model pretraining beyond next-token prediction. Code: https://github.com/haihuang-ml/structure-residual

2611.23030.abs: Not every perception error changes the planner's action. Yet adaptive-resolution perception chooses where to spend high-resolution computation from image cues, which can neither reliably point to an object that low resolution missed nor tell which objects matter to the planner. We observe that the planner can say where an object would matter before anything is seen: inserting a hypothetical object at a location tests whether its action would change. Decision-Guided Speculative Perception (DGSP) treats the low-resolution scene and its action as a draft and probes the planner in this way to obtain a decision-sensitivity field, the locations where an unseen object would change the action. Only this field and the support, the detections on which the current action rests, are verified at high resolution, repeatedly until the action is stable. For two planner classes, we prove that DGSP returns exactly the action of whole-frame high-resolution perception if crop detections match whole-frame ones and the crops cover the field, conditions that real images meet approximately. On three driving datasets, it reproduces this action on about 98% of frames with about a quarter of the pixels. At the pixel cost of uniform downscaling, it repairs more of the draft's disagreements with this action, brakes falsely less often, and recovers many more of the decision-relevant objects that the draft misses.

2611.23129.abs: Advection-diffusion priors are a common way to make neural sea surface temperature (SST) forecasts physics-informed. We test where such a prior must enter a heteroscedastic ConvLSTM to help, using daily NOAA OISST v2.1 for the Bay of Bengal (1982-2024) and a synthetic benchmark on the same grid with known currents of controlled strength. (i) On real data, a soft advection-diffusion residual with a learned velocity gives no reliable benefit (lead-15 CRPS -0.007 degrees C, 95% interval [-0.022, +0.008]); a plain temporal-smoothness penalty matches it, and equivalence within 3% is not established either. (ii) Learned velocities do not recover the currents, whether placed in the loss, in an explicit transport step, or in a transport step without neural correction: they correlate with the reference no better than a shuffled-date null, even on synthetic data where knowing the currents would improve day-15 forecasts by 16-23%. (iii) Supplied currents help on synthetic data, but mostly as information: giving them to the network as input channels, without transport, recovers 92% of the transport design's lead-5 gain, and a frozen-current numerical forecast does as well as either. (iv) With GLORYS12 reanalysis currents on real data, the transport design is 6% and 4% worse at leads 1 and 5; reanalysis advection explains essentially none of the daily OISST change (correlation 0.02), and frozen-current transport is worse than persistence. (v) The defect that matters is lead-dependent miscalibration shared by every model. One variance multiplier per lead, fitted on validation data,…

2611.22382.abs: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream and propose RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), a prompting framework that works through the pages as a reader would: within a sliding window it reasons about each page and commits its boundary decision before moving on, and across windows it carries forward a compact record of what it has read, keeping per-call cost bounded. We also introduce FinancePSS-205, a benchmark of 205 real-world, de-identified financial page streams, to be released publicly. On FinancePSS-205, RICoT matches or outperforms pairwise and windowed prompting with the same backbone for each of three open-weight LLMs; on a TABME test subset, RICoT with GLM-5 reaches document F1 0.847 and boundary F1 0.915, above published zero-shot results. A 2B-parameter student, trained on a larger teacher's decisions with and without the page-level reasoning, performs comparably in both modes and comes within 0.05 document F1 of the strongest prompted model on FinancePSS-205.

ov.problema: I grandi modelli linguistici hanno rinnovato l'interesse per la segmentazione di flussi di pagine (PSS), ovvero dividere un file multi-pagina nei documenti che lo compongono. Tuttavia, i metodi LLM pubblicati inquadrano ancora il compito come classificazione di confine su una o poche pagine vicine, e le API commerciali di divisione documenti non divulgano i loro metodi.
ov.idea: Gli autori reimmaginano la PSS per LLM come un processo sequenziale sull'intero flusso e propongono RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), un framework di prompting che procede attraverso le pagine come farebbe un lettore: entro una finestra scorrevole ragiona su ogni pagina e prende la decisione di confine prima di passare oltre, e tra finestre porta avanti un record compatto di ciò che ha letto, mantenendo il costo per chiamata limitato. Introducono anche FinancePSS-205, un benchmark di 205 flussi di pagine finanziarie reali de-identificate, che sarà rilasciato pubblicamente.
